args.summary:
On September 3, 2021, the Chinese Ministry of Education (教育部) held a press conference announcing the results of the Eighth National Student Physical Fitness and Health Survey (第八次全国学生体质与健康调研). The survey found that the overall physical fitness and health of Chinese students has improved, with the most notable improvements among junior high school students.

Key findings from the survey:
- The national rate of students (ages 6-22) meeting physical fitness excellence standards (体质健康达标优良率) reached 23.8% in 2019.
- For students aged 13-22, the excellence rate rose from 14.8% in 2014 to 17.7% in 2019, an increase of 2.9 percentage points. By age group: students aged 13-15 rose 5.1 points, 16-18 rose 1.8 points, and 19-22 rose only 0.2 points. Junior high school students showed the greatest improvement (5.1 points), while university students improved the least.
- Physical development indicators (height, weight, chest circumference) continued to improve across all age groups.
- Lung capacity levels rose overall over the past 10 years, with the most significant gains among junior high students.
- Flexibility, strength, speed, and endurance improved for primary and junior high students but showed no significant improvement among university students.
- Malnutrition has continued to decline; the malnutrition rate for students aged 6-22 was 10.2% in 2019.

Policy factors driving improvements (per the Ministry's official): 
1. Construction of sports-featured schools, including campus football (校园足球) programs launched in 2015. Students at campus football schools had an excellence rate of 29.2% versus 22.3% at non-football schools.
2. Strengthened physical education exams in the high school entrance examination (中考体育) increased exercise time among middle school students. 42.7% of ninth graders exercised at least one hour daily at school (vs. 30.6% of first-year high schoolers), and ninth graders had an excellence rate of 29.2% (vs. 22.6% for first-year high schoolers).

Family and school factors were also influential: students with parental support had higher excellence rates, and schools meeting physical education class quotas and scheduling two or more eye exercises (眼保健操) daily saw better outcomes. Students exercising 1+ hours daily at school had an excellence rate of 27.4% (vs. 17.7% for insufficient exercise), and students with adequate sleep had a myopia rate of 47.8% (vs. 67.8% for sleep-deprived students).

Persisting problems identified include: high rates of poor vision and myopia, rising overweight/obesity rates, declining grip strength, and declining physical fitness among university students.

Background on the survey: National student physical fitness surveys have been conducted every 5 years since 1985 (2nd-7th surveys in 1991, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014). The eighth survey was organized in 2019 by the Ministry of Education, General Administration of Sport, National Health Commission, National Ethnic Affairs Commission, Ministry of Science and Technology, and Ministry of Finance. Using stratified cluster random sampling, it covered 374,257 students across 1,258 schools in 93 cities in 31 provinces (autonomous regions/municipalities) and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, encompassing full-time regular primary, middle, and higher education institutions.

# 第八次全国学生体质与健康调研显示：我国学生体质与健康状况总体改善 初中生最明显

*![](//n.sinaimg.cn/sinakd10200/360/w180h180/20221208/e06e-657cfe96d386ab6220bec05f8471ef57.jpg)* 

## 中国教育新闻网

[关注](javascript:void(0))

![](//k.sinaimg.cn/n/spider20210903/268/w640h428/20210903/09a0-d735f9a20940a0afd9e8044752ceb0b0.jpg/w300h300z1l10t10q1001ce.jpg)

原标题：第八次全国学生体质与健康调研显示：我国学生体质与健康状况总体改善 初中生最明显 来源：中国教育新闻网

中国教育报-中国教育新闻网北京9月3日讯（记者 欧媚 林焕新）教育部今天召开新闻发布会，公布第八次全国学生体质与健康调研结果。结果显示，我国学生体质与健康状况总体改善，初中生改善最为明显。

 [![](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAQAAAADAQMAAACOOjyFAAAAA1BMVEUAAACnej3aAAAAAXRSTlMAQObYZgAAAApJREFUCNdjAAMAAAYAAegKKqQAAAAASUVORK5CYII=) ![](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAQAAAADAQMAAACOOjyFAAAAA1BMVEUAAACnej3aAAAAAXRSTlMAQObYZgAAAApJREFUCNdjAAMAAAYAAegKKqQAAAAASUVORK5CYII=)](JavaScript:void(0)) 

9月3日，教育部召开2021教育金秋系列第五场新闻发布会。图为发布会现场。（教育部网站）

调研结果显示，学生体质健康达标优良率逐渐上升，2019年全国6-22岁学生体质健康达标优良率为23.8%。13-22岁年龄段学生优良率从2014年的14.8%上升到2019年的17.7%，上升了2.9个百分点，其中，13—15岁、16—18岁、19—22岁学生体质健康达标优良率分别上升5.1、1.8和0.2个百分点。初中生上升最为明显，上升5.1个百分点，大学生上升最少。

学生身高、体重、胸围等形态发育指标持续向好，各年龄组男女生身高、体重、胸围指标均继续呈现上升趋势。

学生肺活量水平全面上升。近10年来，全国学生肺活量持续增加，初中生增长最为明显。

中小学生柔韧、力量、速度和耐力等素质总体出现好转，柔韧素质、力量素质小学生和初中生改善较其他年龄段明显，大学生没有明显改善。

学生营养不良持续改善。2019年我国6—22岁学生营养不良率为10.2%，近10年来，各年龄段男女生营养不良状况持续改善。

教育部体卫艺司负责人介绍，政策措施牵引是促进学生体质与健康水平提高的主要因素之一。一是校园足球等体育特色学校建设促进学生体质与健康。教育部从2015年开始在全国广泛开展体育特色学校建设，对增强学生体质与健康起到了积极作用。校园足球特色学校学生体质健康达标优良率为29.2%，高于非校园足球特色学校的22.3%。

二是中考体育的强化增加中学生体育活动时间。近年来，随着中考体育考试分值提高，中学生尤其是初三学生体育活动时间显著增加。在校体育锻炼1小时比率，初三学生为42.7%，高于高一学生的30.6%。体质健康达标优良率初三学生为29.2%，高于高一学生的22.6%。

此次调研也发现，家庭和学校的教育与引导对提高学生健康素养起着至关重要的作用。得到父母支持的孩子体质健康达标优良率高于没有得到父母支持的学生。同时，学校体育锻炼安排和用眼卫生指导等至关重要，每周体育与健康课课时达标的学校学生体质健康达标优良率显著高于其他学校，每天安排2次以上眼保健操的学校的学生近视风险低于其他学校。

学生保证每天足量的体育锻炼和睡眠时间等对增强身体素质、预防超重肥胖和近视发生有积极影响。每天能够保证1小时以上在校体育锻炼时间的学生体质健康达标优良率为27.4%，显著高于体育锻炼时间不足的学生的17.7%，每天睡眠充足学生的近视率为47.8%，显著低于睡眠不足的学生的67.8%。

此次调研也发现了学生视力不良和近视率偏高、学生超重肥胖率上升、学生握力水平有所下降、大学生身体素质下滑等一些学生体质与健康状况亟待解决的问题。

教育部于2021年9月3日在北京召开新闻发布会（记者欧媚、林焕新），公布第八次全国学生体质与健康调研结果。结果显示，我国学生体质与健康状况总体改善，初中生改善最为明显。具体数据：2019年全国6-22岁学生体质健康达标优良率为23.8%；13-22岁年龄段优良率从2014年的14.8%上升至2019年的17.7%，其中13-15岁上升5.1个百分点（最明显）、16-18岁上升1.8个百分点、19-22岁上升0.2个百分点，大学生上升最少。

其他主要发现包括：学生身高、体重、胸围等形态发育指标持续向好；肺活量水平全面上升（初中生最明显）；中小学生柔韧、力量、速度、耐力素质总体好转（大学生无明显改善）；营养不良状况持续改善（2019年6-22岁学生营养不良率为10.2%）。

教育部体卫艺司负责人指出，政策措施牵引是促进学生体质健康水平提高的主要因素：一是校园足球等体育特色学校建设（特色学校优良率29.2%，高于非特色学校的22.3%）；二是中考体育强化增加中学生体育活动时间（在校锻炼1小时率初三学生42.7%高于高一学生的30.6%，优良率初三29.2%高于高一22.6%）。

调研还显示，家庭和学校教育与引导至关重要——得到父母支持的学生优良率更高；体育课课时达标学校的学生优良率显著更高；每天安排2次以上眼保健操的学校学生近视风险更低。每天保证1小时以上在校锻炼的学生优良率为27.4%（高于不足者的17.7%）；睡眠充足学生近视率47.8%（低于睡眠不足者的67.8%）。

### **摘要**

教育资源应与人口变化相适应，这直接关系到教育强国目标的实现。运用文献研究法、数据分析等研究方法，基于小学和初中体育学科特定周课时与体育教师周课时量的测算，预测2025—2035年间我国义务教育阶段体育教师各年度的需求量，判断各年度体育教师数量的余缺状况。经研究认为：1）2025—2035年间义务教育阶段体育教师需求量随着年份的增长呈现下降趋势。基于A方案，2025—2035年间我国义务教育阶段体育教师需求量为114.28万人至77.25万人；基于B方案，2025—2035年间我国义务教育阶段体育教师需求量为99.46万人至67.25万人。2）基于A 方案，2025—2035年间义务教育阶段体育教师需求量存在缺口与过剩并存的现象，从2031年开始，义务教育阶段体育教师数量开始出现过剩；基于B 方案，2025—2035年间小学体育教师需求量存在缺口与过剩并存的现象，小学自2029年开始出现过剩，初中从2025年就开始出现过剩。基于测算数据，对我国义务教育下一阶段的体育师资配置建议为：严格依据教育部有关规定配备专任体育教师、基于高质量与适度原则调整体育师范生培养规模、基于实践需要弹性调配体育师资布局、做好义务教育阶段体育师资动态配置的预警监测、探索义务教育阶段体育教师退出办法。

### **Abstract**

By applying research methods such as literature review and data analysis, and based on the calculation methods of specific weekly class hours of physical education courses in primary and junior high schools and the weekly class hours of physical education teachers, the demand for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage in China in each year from 2025 to 2035 was predicted, and the surplus and shortage status of physical education teachers in each year was determined. The research suggests that: 1) The demand for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage will show a downward trend as the years go by from 2025 to 2035. Based on the total Plan A, the demand range for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage in China from 2025 to 2035 is between 1.1428 million and 772,500. Based on the combined Plan B, the demand range for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage in China from 2025 to 2035 is between 994,600 and 672,500. 2) Based on the total Plan A, there will be a coexistence of “shortage” and “excess” in the demand for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage from 2025 to 2035. Starting from 2031, the number of physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage will begin to show an excess. Based on the combined Plan B, there will be a coexistence of “shortage” and “surplus” in the demand for physical education teachers. Surplus will occur in primary schools starting from 2029, and in junior high schools, it has already occurred in 2025. Based on the calculated data of the demand for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage, the suggestions for the allocation of physical education teachers in China’s compulsory education stage in the next stage are as follows: Strictly follow the relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education to allocate full-time physical education teachers, moderately adjust the scale of physical education normal student training based on quality, flexibly balance the allocation of physical education teachers based on practical needs, do a good job in early warning and monitoring the dynamic allocation of physical education teachers in compulsory education, and explore the exit methods for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage.

| [22] | 乔锦忠, 沈敬轩, 李汉东, 等. 2020—2035年我国义务教育阶段资源配置研究[J]. 华东师范大学学报(教育科学版), 2021,39(12):59-80.  <https://doi.org/10.16382/j.cnki.1000-5560.2021.12.005>  [本文引用 [1]](javascript:;) 摘要  教育事业发展需要有前瞻性，在《中国教育现代化2035》目标的指引下，有必要对2020—2035期间，我国义务教育阶段的学龄人口变动情况及其对教育资源配置的影响进行深入研究。本研究采用Leslie矩阵的队列要素法和实地访谈法，对2020—2035年期间我国义务教育阶段在校生数、学校数、教师数和所需经费等进行了预测，结果显示：随着生育率和出生人口下降，我国义务教育阶段学生人数呈现出持续下降趋势；与2020年预测值相比，2035年我国义务教育阶段在校生总量将下降约3000万；按现行学校规模计算，2026年（峰值年份）城区需新建小学4000所，2030年（峰值年份）城区需新建初中4000所，农村地区将有大量小学校舍闲置（3.73万）；按现行师生比计算，义务教育阶段专任教师的需求量在下降，与2020年相比，2035年小学教师过剩约150万，初中过剩约37万。2031年，我国城区义务教育学生数将超过镇区，义务教育将总体进入以城市教育为主体的时代，教育资源配置应因地制宜，因时而动，充分考虑学生由农村向镇区和城区的转移。建议科学规划学校布局；适当提高办学标准，降低生师比，缩小班级规模，及时补充优秀教师；统筹优化学前、托育和义务教育阶段的教师资源配置，不断优化教师队伍结构。 |

args.summary:
This webpage presents the academic article "Demand Forecasting and Suggestions on the Physical Education Teachers in the Compulsory Education Stage in China from 2025 to 2035 under the Background of the Decline in School-age Population" (学龄人口减少背景下我国2025—2035年义务教育阶段体育教师需求量预测及建议), authored by SHANG Lipei (尚力沛), Associate Professor at the Institute of Physical Education Curriculum and Teaching, Nanjing Normal University. The article was published in the Journal of Capital University of Physical Education and Sports (首都体育学院学报), 2025, Vol. 37, Issue 5, pages 473-482, with DOI: 10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001. It was received on 2025-08-28 and published online on 2025-11-06.

METHODOLOGY: The study uses literature review and data analysis methods, calculating demand based on specific weekly class hours for physical education in primary and junior high schools combined with weekly class hours per PE teacher.

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Demand for PE teachers in compulsory education will show a downward trend from 2025 to 2035 due to declining school-age population.
2. Under Plan A: demand ranges from 1.1428 million (2025) down to 772,500 (2035) teachers.
3. Under Plan B: demand ranges from 994,600 (2025) down to 672,500 (2035) teachers.
4. Under Plan A, both shortage and excess coexist, with excess beginning in 2031.
5. Under Plan B, primary schools begin to show surplus starting in 2029, while junior high schools already show surplus starting in 2025.

RECOMMENDATIONS for PE teacher allocation: strictly follow Ministry of Education regulations to allocate full-time PE teachers; moderately adjust the scale of PE teacher training based on quality; flexibly balance PE teacher allocation based on practical needs; implement early warning and monitoring of dynamic teacher allocation; and explore exit mechanisms for compulsory education PE teachers.

The article includes 26 references in Chinese, covering topics such as the 7th National Population Census data, the Education Power Nation Construction Plan (2024-2035), national education statistics, and prior studies on teacher resource allocation. Classification: G807 (Physical Education).

# 教育部办公厅 财政部办公厅 关于做好2025年农村义务教育阶段学校 教师特设岗位计划实施工作的通知

教师厅〔2025〕1号

有关省、自治区、直辖市教育厅（教委）、财政厅（局），新疆生产建设兵团教育局、财政局：

　　为全面落实《教育强国建设规划纲要（2024—2035年）》，推进落实《中共中央 国务院关于弘扬教育家精神加强新时代高素质专业化教师队伍建设的意见》，加强农村教师队伍建设，推动乡村教育高质量发展，实现巩固拓展脱贫攻坚成果同乡村振兴有效衔接，现就做好2025年农村义务教育阶段学校教师特设岗位计划（以下简称“特岗计划”）实施工作通知如下。

**一、政策要点**

　　（一）实施范围。2025年“特岗计划”实施范围为：原集中连片特殊困难地区、中西部国家扶贫开发工作重点县和省级扶贫开发工作重点县，西部地区原“两基”攻坚县（含新疆生产建设兵团的部分团场），纳入国家西部开发计划的部分中部省份的少数民族自治州以及西部地区一些有特殊困难的边境县、少数民族自治县和少小民族县。

　　（二）招聘数量。2025年全国计划招聘“特岗计划”教师20976名，各省（区、市）和新疆生产建设兵团的招聘名额见2025年“特岗计划”各地设岗名额分配表（附件）。

　　（三）招聘条件。1.符合招聘岗位要求，具有相应的教师资格证书，应符合《中华人民共和国教师法》《教师资格条例》等法律法规规定的普通话水平、身体条件和心理条件。符合新时代中小学教师职业行为十项准则要求，无刑事犯罪记录和其他不得聘用的违法记录。2.一般要求本科及以上学历，以师范类专业为主。3.年龄不超过32周岁。4.参加过“大学生志愿服务西部计划”、有从教经历的志愿者和参加过半年以上实习支教的师范院校毕业生同等条件下优先录取。5.支持鼓励符合条件的优秀退役军人、优秀退役运动员到中小学任教，可综合考虑服役年限等因素相应放宽年龄限制。

　　（四）工作重点。重点向原“三区三州”、国家乡村振兴重点帮扶县、少数民族地区等地区倾斜；持续优化教师队伍结构，进一步加强道德与法治、体育与健康、外语、科学、劳动、艺术、信息科技、心理健康、特殊教育等紧缺薄弱学科教师的补充。

**二、工作要求**

　　（一）科学统筹特岗教师招聘。各地要严格按照核定的岗位数量，结合本地实际情况，及时广泛发布招聘信息，提前安排招聘报名、考试、考察、体检等时间表，确保7月底前完成招聘工作。要增强招聘考试针对性、科学性，提高命题工作质量，体现“干什么、考什么”，突出对教师专业素质和教学能力的考察，有条件、有需要的地方可以进行专业能力测试。边远艰苦地区和急需紧缺专业的特岗教师招聘，可结合实际适当降低或不设开考比例，采取面试、直接考察的方式公开招聘，划定成绩合格线。对于特别边远艰苦、教师流失较严重的地区可向本地生源倾斜。鼓励以“双一流”建设高校为代表的高水平高校为农村学校输送教育情怀深厚、专业素养卓越、教学基本功扎实的优秀毕业生。在“特岗计划”招聘基础上，根据具体需要，统筹做好地方特岗教师招聘工作。

　　（二）系统开展特岗教师培训。各地要对标教育强国建设规划目标，围绕高素质专业化教师队伍建设，制定培训规划，为特岗教师提供高质量的培训研修服务。强化教育家精神引领，将师德师风和教育家精神融入教师培训全过程，规范教师从教行为，落实立德树人根本任务；加强岗前职后培训，按照特岗教师实际需求优化培训内容和方式，开展针对性的教育和培训，鼓励将特岗教师纳入当地各级名师工作室进行重点培养；加强非师范专业特岗教师教育教学技能培训，提升教育教学基本素质与能力。

　　（三）严格规范特岗教师管理。加强留任管理，严格按照有关文件精神，保证三年服务期满、考核合格且愿意留任的特岗教师及时入编并落实工作岗位，做好相关人事、工资关系等接转工作，连续计算工龄、教龄，不再实行试用期，做好服务证书编制和发放工作。加强信息管理，教育部将继续把“全国教师管理信息系统”数据作为“特岗计划”实施情况、核定招聘计划、特岗教师硕士研究生考试加分资格的基础数据。各地要扎实做好数据录入和更新工作，地方特岗计划有关信息纳入数据录入范围，确保数据库完整准确。

　　（四）做好特岗教师待遇保障。中央财政继续对“特岗计划”教师给予工资性补助，标准为西部地区年人均4.18万元，中部地区年人均3.88万元。教育部、财政部将根据各地2025年设岗计划和往届特岗教师在岗人数核拨2025年“特岗计划”中央补助经费。各地要强化主体责任，确保特岗教师工资按时足额发放，按规定参加社会保险，同等条件下在薪酬待遇、职称评聘、评先评优、年度考核等方面享受与当地公办学校在编教师同等待遇。按照国家有关规定落实好服务期满特岗教师相关优惠政策。落实好周转宿舍等安排，帮助解决特岗教师工作生活中的实际困难。

　　（五）加强实施工作推进指导。各地要严格实施“特岗计划”，落实教师待遇保障政策，加大对按照核定计划和岗位要求开展教师招聘、特岗教师工资按时足额发放、“五险一金”缴纳和服务期满留任特岗教师入编手续及时办理等情况的摸排力度，并抓好政策落实。各地在摸清拟设岗县教师队伍实际情况和需求的基础上，认真研究提出2026年实施“计划”的县（市）、学校和特设岗位教师数量，并于2025年12月31日前通过全国教师管理信息系统报送。

　　附件：[2025年“特岗计划”各地设岗名额分配表](./W020250523520565767210.docx)

args.summary:
This is an official notice (教师厅〔2025〕1号) jointly issued by the General Offices of China's Ministry of Education and Ministry of Finance (dated May 8, 2025) regarding the implementation of the 2025 "Special Post Plan" (特岗计划) for rural compulsory education school teachers.

KEY POLICY POINTS:
- Scope: Covers former contiguous special hardship areas, national/provincial poverty-alleviation key counties in central/western China, western "两基" counties, minority autonomous prefectures in central provinces under western development, and special-needs border/minority counties.
- Recruitment quota: 20,976 teachers nationwide in 2025 (detailed quotas per province in attached allocation table).
- Eligibility: Must have teaching certificates and meet legal requirements (Teacher Law, Teacher Qualification Regulations); generally requires bachelor's degree or above, mainly normal (teacher-training) majors; age not exceeding 32 years (veterans and retired athletes may have relaxed age limits with consideration for service years); no criminal records. Preference for Western Plan volunteers, those with teaching experience, and normal graduates with 6+ months of teaching internship. Outgoing teachers should be placed in shortage subjects like moral/legal education, physical education, foreign languages, science, labor, arts, information technology, mental health, and special education.

WORK REQUIREMENTS:
1. Recruitment: Hiring must be completed by end of July 2025; exams should test professional and teaching competency; remote hardship areas may lower/waive exam ratios or use interviews/direct assessment; encourages high-level universities ("双一流") to send outstanding graduates.
2. Training: Comprehensive training programs aligned with education-power building goals; integrate educator spirit and teacher ethics; strengthen pre/post-service training and skills training for non-normal program teachers; encourage inclusion in local master teacher studios.
3. Management: Three-year service period teachers who pass assessment and choose to stay must be promptly placed into permanent establishment (入编) with continuous service/seniority calculation, no probation period; data maintained in the National Teacher Management Information System (also used for postgrad exam score bonus eligibility).
4. Compensation: Central government salary subsidy: 41,800 yuan/person/year in western regions; 38,800 yuan/person/year in central regions; salaries must be paid on time with social insurance; equal treatment with local public school in-service teachers in pay, professional title evaluation, honors, and annual assessment; implement post-service preferential policies and provide temporary housing.
5. Guidance/Deadline: Localities must submit 2026 plan county/school/position proposals via the National Teacher Management Information System by December 31, 2025.

The notice cites the Education Power-Building Planning Outline (2024-2035) and the CPC Central Committee/State Council opinion on strengthening high-quality professional teacher teams as its policy basis.

　　二是积极发挥地方政府专项债券的保障作用。去年，国家优化完善了地方政府专项债券管理机制，扩大了地方政府专项债券的支持范围，高等教育、职业教育等领域的项目都可以申请地方政府专项债券。国家发展改革委将继续指导地方师范类高等院校、职业院校申报地方政府专项债券，将更多师范院校符合条件的项目纳入支持范围。

args.summary:
This webpage is the live transcript of a Ministry of Education (MOE) press conference held on September 5, 2025, at 10:00 AM in Beijing, marking the first anniversary of the National Education Conference and the upcoming 41st Teachers' Day (September 10, 2025). The conference was moderated by Chen Xing (Deputy Director of MOE General Office and Director of the Press Office). Speakers included Yu Weiye (Director of MOE Teacher Work Department), Ma Hongbing (Deputy Director of Ministry of Finance Science, Education, Culture and Tourism Department), Zhai Jianmin (NDRC Social Department Human Resources Development Director), Hong Jun (Xiamen Education Bureau Deputy Director), Li Qing (Central China Normal University AI Education Department teacher), and Fei Zhenhong (Qixia Experimental Middle School teacher, Shandong).

Key information presented:
- **Teacher Honors**: Wang Zhenyi (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) received the "Republic Medal"; Zhang Jinfan and Huang Danian received the "People's Educator" national honor titles (second batch after Yu Yi, Wei Xinghua, Gao Mingxuan).
- **Teacher development (Ministry of Education)**: First batch of "National Excellent Program" (国优计划) graduates joined primary/secondary schools; normal university public-funded education upgraded from bachelor's to graduate level; nearly 10,000 "Excellent Teacher Program" (优师计划) first graduates entered western/less-developed areas.
- **Teacher numbers (Ministry of Finance)**: In 2024, China had nearly 19 million full-time teachers (up by over 1.5 million from 2019). Central finance allocated 16 billion yuan for teacher training during the 14th Five-Year Plan and nearly 45 billion yuan for teacher development in central/western regions.
- **Key statistics**: 2024 vocational college "dual-qualified" (双师型) teacher ratio reached 58% (up 23 percentage points from 2019); 120+ million rural teachers benefit from living subsidies annually; public-funded education trains 8,000+ teachers yearly for central/western regions; "Excellent Teacher Program" trains ~10,000 annually for 832 poverty-alleviation counties; "Special Post Program" added ~250,000 rural teachers over 5 years.
- **NDRC investment**: Over 100 billion yuan central budget investment for school construction (including rural teacher housing); starting new higher education student dormitory capacity (for the student population peak approaching higher education); equipment renewal via ultra-long-term special treasury bonds.
- **41st Teachers' Day theme**: "Cultivating the soul with educator spirit, writing a glorious chapter of education power building" (以教育家精神铸魂强师，谱写教育强国建设华章).
- **Respect/benefit policies**: National-level "Respect Teachers, Benefit Teachers" (尊师惠师) policies launched covering healthcare, transport, consumption, and tourism; "China Teacher" mini-program launched with electronic work permits for discounts; second phase of "Respect Teachers Benefit Teachers Public Welfare Action" launched in August 2025, covering office software, housing, cars, daily goods, entertainment, dining, and transport.
- **Xiamen progress**: Obtained 6,000 teacher positions from provincial government; implemented "same city, same salary, same staffing" policy for rural/island teachers; established wage linkage between teachers and civil servants.
- **Central China Normal University**: Self-developed "Xiaoya" cloud platform and "Shishuo" (师说) teacher education large model (trained on 20,000+ classroom videos), honored as a national "AI + Higher Education" typical application case.
- **NDRC future plans (15th Five-Year Plan)**: Use three funding channels (central budget investment/"two-heavy" funds, local government special bonds, equipment renewal funds) to support teacher education capacity.
- **International engagement**: Global Teacher Development College established at Beijing Normal University with 22 branches; Education Minister Huai Jinpeng attended World Teacher Summit in Chile, sharing China's teacher development experience.

# 国家加大对农村教育扶持力度 缩小城乡教育差距

　　1月12日下午，纲要工作小组办公室成员、中央教科所所长袁振国；纲要基础教育专题组成员、教育部基础司一司副司长王定华；纲要总体战略组成员、中国教育报副总编翟博；纲要促进教育公平战略组成员、中央教科所教育政策研究中心主任吴霓；纲要促进教育公平战略组成员、中央教科所全国教学科学规划办公室副主任曾天山做客新华网谈把促进教育公平作为我国基本教育政策。

**[主持人]众所周知，我国农村人口数量占到全国人口数的70%，可见他们的教育问题是会影响整个国家教育发展水平的关键所在。但是很多农村孩子上学条件差、师资力量不强也都是不容回避的现实。在推进城市化建设中，如何缩小城乡间教育差距保障农村学生平等受教育权益？**

**[王定华]**党中央、国务院十分重视农村教育，采取很多切实的措施加大对农村教育的扶持力度，应该说这些年农村教育取得了巨大的、历史性的成绩。我们已经在全国99.3%的人口地区普及了九年义务教育，实际上这些年的普九主要就是在发展农村教育。小学的入学率已经实现了100%，男女童的入学率没有任何差异。而且农村的高中教育也有了比较大的发展，将有力地促进全国高中阶段教育的普及。

　　同时，农村的职业教育提倡以服务为宗旨，“以就业为导向，以工学合作为主要模式”，采取订单式培养等各种方式大力发展农村职业教育，特别是农村中等职业技术教育，成效非常显著。

　　另外办学的条件也发生了巨大的变化，有人说“过去进村看学校要到土地庙，现在进村看学校楼房高耸红旗飘”，这也是真实的写照。特别是从2003年启动、2004年大面积铺开的“西部两基攻坚计划”，面对西部广袤农村地区大力加大教育普及和质量的提高，现在在这些农村地区最漂亮的建筑就是中小学校园，西部有些年轻人结婚愿意到校园里拍婚纱照，有些寄宿制学校的食堂改善得好了，孩子们周末都不愿意回家，想在学校吃饭。所以我们必须肯定这个变化是很大的。

　　但是由于特殊的经济社会的原因，特别是长期的城乡二元结构的现实影响，再加上一些农村地区自然条件也比较差，所以总体上农村教育落后的面貌还没有得到根本的改变。因此，我们以后还要继续加大对农村教育的扶持，从办学条件上我们要制定城乡统一的办学标准，而且这个办学标准比以前城市和乡村都要高。把中小学建设成为当地最结实、最漂亮的公共设施。成为一旦发生地震等自然灾害的当地群众的第一避难所。

　　二是要统一城市、县镇和农村教师的编制标准，而且要就高不就低；三是加大对农村教师培训的力度，这是非常关键的。提高教师的水平成为制约农村教育质量高低的关键因素，广大教师教书育人质量必须要合格。但是我们现在农村还有24万名教师没有达到国家规定的合格学历，还有将近38万名代课人员，所以他们的水平有待于提高，因此要加大对农村教师的培训。

　　同时，在这个过程中我们要继续推进免费师范生的试点，继续实行中西部农村教师特色岗位计划，吸引优秀的青年从事教育工作，到西部去，到农村去。同时，为了加大对农村教育的支持力度，我们也鼓励东部地区、发达地区派老师、出资金，或者通过其他方式搞手拉手的对农村的扶持。还有一点，对农村教育要进行课程开发上的指导，使农村课程真正切合农村学生的实际，同时又让农村学生的基础知识、技能、品德有所提升。地方课程、学校课程要有利于农村的实际。通过我们的努力，我想再过几年城乡教育的差距会得到有效的缩小。

（责任编辑 王朋）

This webpage is a transcript of a January 12 press interview hosted by Xinhua Net, featuring officials from China's Education Ministry and the Central Institute for Educational Sciences. The discussion focused on China's national policy to strengthen support for rural education and narrow the urban-rural education gap, treating the promotion of educational equity as a fundamental national education policy.

Key participants included: Yuan Zhenguo (Director of the Central Institute for Educational Sciences and member of the Outline Working Group), Wang Dinghua (Deputy Director of the First Department of Basic Education, Ministry of Education), Zhai Bo (Deputy Chief Editor of China Education Daily), Wu Ni (Director, Education Policy Research Center), and Zeng Tianshan (Deputy Director, National Teaching Science Planning Office).

Wang Dinghua reported significant achievements in rural education, noting that nine-year compulsory education has been popularized in areas covering 99.3% of China's population, primary school enrollment has reached 100%, and there is no gender gap in enrollment. Rural vocational education has developed through employment-oriented and work-study models. Since the "Western Two-Basics" (two basics) project launched in 2003 and expanded in 2004, rural schools have become the most beautiful buildings in their regions.

However, Wang acknowledged rural education still lags due to historical urban-rural dual structure and poor natural conditions. Proposed measures include: (1) establishing unified urban-rural school standards (higher than previous standards) and constructing schools as the sturdiest local public facilities and earthquake shelters; (2) unifying urban, county, and rural teacher staffing standards at the higher level; (3) strengthening teacher training—currently 240,000 rural teachers lack qualified credentials and nearly 380,000 substitute teachers need improvement; (4) continuing free normal-student pilots and the central/western rural teacher special post program; (5) encouraging eastern developed regions to support rural areas; and (6) developing rural-specific curricula to fit local realities.

## “特岗计划”实施20年来约120万教师坚守农村讲台，广大教师不断将教育家精神转化为思想行动自觉——

# 以教师之强筑牢教育强国根基

　　2025年9月8日，在第41个教师节来临之际，习近平总书记给全国特岗教师代表回信，他勉励大家继续坚守教育初心，不断提高教书育人本领，用心用情呵护引导孩子们健康成长，努力培养出更多德智体美劳全面发展的社会主义建设者和接班人，为推进乡村振兴、建设教育强国作出新的贡献。

　　党的二十大报告提出，深入实施科教兴国战略、人才强国战略、创新驱动发展战略；加快建设教育强国、科技强国、人才强国。

　　教育强国建设是支撑引领中国式现代化的战略性、先导性工程，教师队伍建设则是教育强国建设最重要的基础工作。

**以教育家精神引领铸造强师队伍**

　　“到祖国和人民最需要的地方去”，“特岗计划”实施20年来，约120万名特岗教师牢记初心使命、扎根乡村教书育人，把最美的年华奉献给了农村学校，有力改善了我国教师队伍结构性短板，大幅提升了农村学校教育教学水平。一个个“言为士则、行为世范”的身影，闪耀着中国特有的教育家精神。

　　有高质量的教师，才会有高质量的教育。

　　当前，我国有一支数量庞大的教师队伍，支撑起世界上最大规模的教育体系。激励广大教师将教育家精神作为自觉追求和行动自觉，甘做燃灯者、争当引路人，教育大国向教育强国迈进的步伐越走越坚定。

　　“教育不是等条件好了再去做，而是带着孩子们一起创造条件。”最近，2025年全国“最美教师”、河南省新乡市封丘县潘店镇大辛庄小学特岗教师任明杰，在他执教的村小里上了一节特别的思政课。

　　在这节由安阳师范学院组织的“榜样引领 师道传承”弘扬教育家精神主题思政课上，任明杰与母校公费师范生、校友教师代表围坐一堂，用10年乡村教育实践诠释教育家精神的真谛。

　　师范生们的分享让思政课更添共鸣。安阳师院化学化工学院学生罗京京对未来职业有了清晰图景：“要让知识因教育的温度而生动。”

　　从黄土高坡到西南边陲，从雪域高原到大漠戈壁，陕西师范大学一批批师范生，用无悔的青春选择书写着“扎根西部、甘于奉献、追求卓越、教育报国”的“西部红烛两代师表”精神。

　　召开教育家精神铸魂强师行动推进会暨2025年教师队伍建设重点工作部署会，强化教育家精神引领，筑牢立德树人根基，引导广大教师践行共同价值，促进自律自强；启动“教育家精神万里行”活动，为教育家精神铸魂强师搭建全新载体；公示2025年全国“最美教师”宣传选树人选及事迹，展现新时代广大人民教师弘扬和践行教育家精神，潜心教书育人、培根铸魂，躬身践行初心使命的生动实践……一年来，教育系统以大力弘扬教育家精神为引领，着力造就一支高素质专业化教师队伍。

　　学高为师，身正为范。

　　教育家精神的高位引领，给教师队伍师德师风建设设定了新的标杆，完善的制度设计则对违背师德、有损教师队伍形象的行为“零容忍”：2025年以来，新时代师德师风建设长效机制意见出台，强化师德师风全链条闭环管理，扎实推进师德师风教育涵养常态化、日常监管制度化、考核评价科学化、规范惩处严格化。

　　以德养身、以德立学、以德施教，在教育家精神的高位引领与新时代师德师风的“刚性约束”下，越来越多的教师有了行动的价值坐标，自觉追求成为“经师”与“人师”相统一的“大先生”已蔚然成风。

**以改革创新开拓强师优师新局面**

　　教师是教育的第一资源，是建设高质量教育体系、实施高质量教育的根本力量。

　　当前，我国有各级各类学校专任教师1885.1万名。建设教育强国，办好人民满意的教育，呼唤更多的教育家型教师。

　　2025年，从小梦想成为一名人民教师的华东师范大学2025届硕士研究生黄温瑞，作为首届“国优计划”毕业生正式走上了中学教师岗位。

　　从数据科学到数学教学，黄温瑞表示，得益于“国优计划”培养体系，自己顺利完成了从技术人才到教育者的角色转变，未来将积极发挥跨学科优势，增强课堂吸引力，引导学生适应人工智能时代。

　　依托高水平大学开展教师教育，折射出新时代教育强国建设对高素质师资的迫切需求。

　　2025年4月，教师教育创新机制改革试点工作部署会在北京召开。作为教育强国建设三年行动计划综合改革首批试点安排之一，会议传递出深化教师教育综合改革，培养造就新时代高水平教师队伍的鲜明信号。

　　“躬耕教坛、强国有我，志存高远、师范报国。”6月28日，在北京师范大学珠海校区风雨操场举行的首届“优师计划”师范生从教出征仪式上，年轻学子的铮铮誓言响彻会场。此后，学校首批368名“优师计划”毕业生奔赴中西部13个省份148个脱贫县和陆地边境县，投身基础教育一线。

　　瞄准中西部基础教育师资结构性短缺和整体素质提升问题，2025年，近万名“优师计划”首届毕业生走上了中西部教育岗位，为当地教育注入新活力。为支持师范生发展，教育部表示将支持“优师计划”师范生职后学历提升。实施“三区”人才支持计划教师专项计划、银龄讲学计划等系列支教项目，结合乡村教育发展实际需求，选派优秀教师到乡村学校支教，促进城乡义务教育优质均衡发展。

　　启动“教师教育能力提升工程”，提出构建教师人才培养新模式、搭建教师教育研究新平台等五大任务，为新时代教师教育体系构建探索新路径……以教育家精神为引领，以改革创新为动能，中国特色教师教育体系不断向高质量迈进。

　　高校教师是发挥高等教育龙头作用的生力军。为优化教师队伍结构，加快高层次复合型人才培养，2025年2月，《普通本科高校产业兼职教师管理办法》印发，围绕产业兼职教师选聘、不同主体工作任务、相关政策支持等方面提出创新举措，充分调动产业兼职教师、普通本科高校、企事业单位参与产教融合的积极性，加强高校产业兼职教师队伍建设。10月，教育部等六部门出台《关于加强新时代高校青年教师队伍建设的指导意见》，聚焦高校青年教师引育管用全链条建设提出创新举措，支持引导青年教师全面发展，提升思想政治素质、教育教学水平、科研创新能力、社会服务本领、国际化视野，推动青年教师不断适应国家战略、科技变革与经济社会发展的新要求，为教育强国、科技强国、人才强国建设提供更为有力的师资保障。

　　当前，人工智能技术已深度融入教育各个环节，从赋能一线教学、助力区域教育公平，到重塑人才培养模式，展现出广泛而深刻的应用前景。

　　从“用起来”到“如何用好”，面对教育数字化深入推进给教师带来的新机遇、新挑战和新要求，启动实施“数字化赋能教师发展行动”，以六大行动提升教师数字素养，开辟教师发展新赛道、塑造教师发展新优势；发布《教师生成式人工智能应用指引（第一版）》，在鼓励应用的同时划出清晰的伦理与操作边界，为教师提供清晰的应用地图和明确的行为边界。

　　聚焦提升教师管理服务效能，升级上线全国教师管理信息系统，将教师系统与教师业务工作紧密结合，构建教师管理、教师服务、专项业务、数据分析四大功能模块体系，深度对接国家教育治理公共服务平台等数据资源，为各级教育行政部门和学校提供“一站式”教师管理服务，提升教师管理精准化和决策科学化水平，助力高水平教师队伍建设。

　　在“优”字上突破、在“新”字上聚力，一年来，为教育强国筑牢根基，教师队伍建设步履不停。

**以制度完善让教师“安心”“安身”**

　　国将兴，必贵师而重傅；贵师而重傅，则法度存。

　　教师的地位高低事关教师工作积极性和职业吸引力，影响着教师队伍的稳定性和整体水平。吸引更多优秀人才热心从教、精心从教、长期从教、终身从教，既需要尊师，也需要惠师。

　　减轻教师负担，让教师把有限的时间精力投入到教书育人的本职工作之中——

　　一年来，中央及地方各级教育部门高度重视教师减负工作，陆续出台一系列相关政策，确保教师主责主业回归教育教学。

　　2025年10月，教育部出台《关于进一步减轻中小学教师非教育教学负担若干措施的通知》，针对教师反映强烈的非教育教学负担重问题，出台8条举措进一步减轻中小学教师非教育教学负担，创设潜心教书、静心育人良好环境，突出源头减负，建立发文前审核，实施减负一致性评估，以机制创新推动教师减负向制度化、规范化、长效化转向。

　　四川省推动教师减负工作制度化，明确每所学校每学期各类进校园活动不得超过6次，鼓励安排教师实行“弹性上下班制”，探索“时间银行”等弹性工作模式。

　　从“案牍劳形”到“轻装育人”，山东省威海市创新通过数字技术赋能教师减负，开发建设“威海市教育数字服务平台”“教育工作者基础数据库”等大数据信息库，为师生提供便捷服务，把时间还给教师。

　　覆盖各级各类教师的待遇保障机制不断完善，尊师惠师政策转化为教师的职业尊荣感和获得感——

　　一年来，各地积极推进教师“公共服务优先”政策，吸引更多力量积极参与尊师惠师行动。

　　2025年3月，“中国教师”服务平台及移动端“中国教师”小程序正式上线，为全国各级各类学校教师提供教师政策资讯、教师培训查询、惠师服务、电子工作证照等多元化服务，强化应用驱动，不断提升服务效率和服务质量，切实增强教师获得感和幸福感。

　　教育部会同国家发展改革委、住房和城乡建设部等部门加强乡村教师住房保障，首次构建“配租+配售”相结合的乡村教师住房保障体系。首次在国家层面围绕医疗、交通、消费、旅游等出台尊师惠师政策，上线“AI教师心理陪伴”，教师待遇保障进入了更加系统、务实的新阶段。

　　青海省海西州建立优秀教师疗休养制度，每年设立专项经费，组织骨干教师、优秀班主任及乡村教师代表开展疗休养活动，教育部门会同文旅部门对教职工免费开放所有旅游景区。

　　浙江省温州市教育局推出“乐师盒”尊师惠师数字平台，教师不用出示教师资格证和身份证，通过个人专属的“尊师二维码”即可便捷享受各类惠师权益，实现“一码通认、一码通享”，吸纳了全市数百家企事业单位参与其中。

　　一项项具体部署瞄准教师“刚需”，既展现制度善意，又充满决策温度；一件件“暖师”举措扎实推进，让教师的获得感、荣誉感、幸福感持续增强。

　　教师是立教之本、兴教之源。今天，尊师惠师政策体系日益完善，“贵师而重傅”的社会氛围日益浓厚，进一步激励着广大教师以教育家精神为引领，用过硬的专业能力、渊博的知识水平、深沉的仁爱之心，承担起培育时代新人的重任，为筑牢教育强国根基、支撑民族复兴伟业注入磅礴而持久的师者力量。（本报记者 梁丹）

This article from the Chinese Ministry of Education (published around September-October 2025) reports on China's efforts to strengthen its teaching workforce to build a strong education system ("教育强国"/education powerhouse). Key developments include:

1. **"特岗计划" (Special Post Plan) 20th Anniversary**: Approximately 1.2 million special-post teachers have served in rural schools over two decades, improving the structural weaknesses of China's teacher workforce and rural education quality.

2. **Educator Spirit (教育家精神) Initiatives**: On September 8, 2025 (the 41st Teachers' Day), President Xi Jinping replied to a letter from national special-post teacher representatives, encouraging them to continue their educational mission and contribute to rural revitalization and building China into an education powerhouse. Activities include the "教育家精神万里行" tour, the 2025 "最美教师" (Most Beautiful Teacher) selections, and a new work conference on implementing educator spirit to strengthen the teaching force.

3. **Teacher Training Reforms**: 
   - The "国优计划" (National Excellent Plan) produced its first graduates, including East China Normal University's Huang Wenrui, who transitioned from data science to mathematics teaching.
   - First cohort of 368 "优师计划" (Excellent Teacher Plan) graduates deployed to 148 poverty-alleviated and border counties across 13 central/western provinces; nearly 10,000 first-cohort graduates took up teaching posts in central/western China in 2025.
   - Teacher education innovation mechanism reform pilot work began April 2025.
   - The "教师教育能力提升工程" (Teacher Education Capacity Improvement Project) launched with five major tasks.

4. **Higher Education Faculty Policies**: 
   - February 2025: 《普通本科高校产业兼职教师管理办法》 (Regulations on Industry Adjunct Teachers for Regular Undergraduate Universities) issued.
   - October 2025: Ministry of Education and five other departments issued guidance on strengthening young university teacher teams.

5. **Digitalization and AI**: Launched "数字化赋能教师发展行动" (Digital Empowerment of Teacher Development Action) with six initiatives; released《教师生成式人工智能应用指引（第一版）》(Guidelines on Generative AI Application for Teachers v1.0); upgraded the national teacher management information system.

6. **Teacher Workload Reduction**: October 2025, the Ministry of Education issued measures with 8 provisions to reduce non-teaching burdens on primary and secondary school teachers. Sichuan limited campus activities to 6 per semester with flexible work schedules; Weihai, Shandong used digital platforms for burden reduction.

7. **Teacher Benefits and Support**: 
   - March 2025: "中国教师" (China Teacher) service platform and mini-program launched.
   - Constructed a "租赁+配售" (rental plus sale) housing security system for rural teachers for the first time.
   - First national-level preferential policies for teachers covering healthcare, transportation, consumption, and tourism; "AI教师心理陪伴" (AI Teacher Psychological Companionship) launched.
   - Examples: Qinghai's Hotan Prefecture established rest/recuperation systems; Wenzhou, Zhejiang launched the "乐师盒" digital platform for teacher benefits.

The article emphasizes that China has 18.851 million full-time teachers in schools of all levels, a number supporting the world's largest education system, and stresses the importance of teachers as the foundation of education building.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This academic paper, published in the Journal of Physical Education (March 2025), analyzes the 'No Less Than 2 Hours of Comprehensive Physical Activity per Day' policy for primary and secondary school students, as stipulated in China's 'Education Strengthening Country Construction Plan Outline (2024-2035)'. The policy represents an evolution from the earlier '1 hour per day' requirement and reflects a deepening national commitment to 'sports-oriented education'. The paper argues the policy is critical for addressing student health issues (e.g., obesity, myopia) and promoting high-quality school physical education.

The paper outlines a collaborative implementation strategy involving schools and families. At the school level (the 'main channel'), it recommends the 'Four Ones': (1) one physical education class per day, (2) one specialized sports skill for each student, (3) one sports team per class, and (4) one tailored implementation plan per school. At the family level (the 'booster'), parents are urged to do the 'Three Things': accompany, supervise, and guide their children's physical activities. The 'comprehensive' nature of the policy requires integration of in-school and out-of-school activities and the seamless connection of teaching, practice, and competition ('teach, practice, compete' model). The paper also discusses challenges such as insufficient PE teachers, lack of sports facilities, and the need for innovative solutions (e.g., converting dining halls into gyms, building rooftop fields). It concludes that successful implementation requires both quality and quantity, and a whole-of-society approach.
</summary>

3. **Class Competitions**: Each semester, primary schools must organize at least 5 class-level competitions, middle schools at least 4, and high schools at least 3, with at least one "three major ball" (football, basketball, volleyball) class competition.

4. **Skill Requirements**: Every student must master at least 2 sports skills by the end of compulsory education. "Three major ball" sports must be included as compulsory content in primary and middle school PE classes.

5. **Teacher Training**: By 2027, all districts must complete a rotation of physical education teacher training. Schools can hire retired teachers and part-time coaches to address staffing shortages.

6. **Facilities**: Primary and middle schools must equip horizontal bars and other fitness equipment by the end of 2025.

7. **Sports-School Partnerships**: Municipal sports schools must partner with at least 2 schools, district sports schools with at least 5 schools, with sports school vice principals serving as deputy principals at partner schools.

8. **Evaluation**: Schools failing to implement measures or showing declining student fitness levels will face inspection and feedback processes.

--- SOURCE 11: 关于落实“中小学生每天综合体育活动时间不低于2小时”工作的思考 ---
URL: https://edu.gmw.cn/2025-03/11/content_37898063.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a scholarly article published in 体育学刊 (Journal of Physical Education) by authors 刘海元 (Liu Haiyuan) and 单舜 (Shan Shun), affiliated respectively with 首都体育学院 (Capital Institute of Physical Education) and 湖南第一师范学院 (Hunan First Normal University). Published March 11, 2025 on Guangming Daily's education channel, the article analyzes the implementation of the policy requiring primary and secondary school students to engage in "no less than 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity per day" (referred to as "2小时" or "2 hours").

## Policy Background (3 sections)

**1. Evolution of daily physical activity time policy (5 stages):**
- Stage 1 (1950s): 1951 State Council decision restricted student activities, recommending 1-1.5 hours of daily physical/recreational activity due to excessive academic workloads threatening health.
- Stage 2 (1978-1990s): After Cultural Revolution, 1978 notice required average 1 hour daily organized exercise; 1990 《学校体育工作条例》 legally mandated 1 hour daily physical activity (including PE classes).
- Stage 3 (2005-2011): Multiple documents (2005, 2006, 2007, 2009 《全民健身条例》, 2011 Government Work Report) clarified that the 1 hour must be on-campus time.
- Stage 4 (2020-present): Shift to requirement of 2 hours daily comprehensive activity (can be on or off campus).
- Stage 5: The 2-hour requirement targeting primary and secondary students (not university students).

**Key policy milestones for the 2-hour requirement:**
- October 2020: 中办国办 document first mentioned ensuring 2 hours daily (1 hour on campus + 1 hour off campus).
- Early 2024: Ministry of Education included "2-hour daily exercise pilot for compulsory education students" in annual work priorities.
- September 26, 2024: Vice Minister of Education 王嘉毅 announced the 2-hour requirement (one PE class daily + 1 hour after-class exercise).
- December 27, 2024: MOE held national school sports reform symposium in Anhui.
- January 2025: 《教育强国建设规划纲要(2024—2035年)》 formally required "中小学生每天综合体育活动时间不低于2小时".

**2. School sports as key content of education power construction:** School sports has political character (part of five-fold education), people's character (affects family well-being), and strategic character (national talent competition). Countries like US, UK, Finland, Australia, Japan are all strengthening school sports.

**3. New education ecosystem creating conditions:** Education structure reform, quality improvements (91.1% preschool enrollment, 95.7% nine-year compulsory education completion, 60.2% higher education enrollment), and "double reduction" policy (双减) freeing up student time. 92.7% of schools conduct arts/sports activities; 90%+ of students voluntarily participate in after-school services.

## Practical Basis (3 sections)

**1. Addressing chronic weakness in student physical fitness:** Despite 4 high-level policy documents over ~40 years (2007, 2012, 2016, 2020), student fitness hasn't fundamentally improved. 2023 national tests showed: 87.1% pass rate (down 2.9 percentage points from 2021), 35.3% excellent rate (down 3.3 points), 12.9% fail rate. Chongqing survey: 64.1% of students exercise less than 1 hour after school; nearly 60% exercise less than 30 minutes daily. Students with 1+ hour daily exercise had 27.4% excellent fitness rate vs 17.7% for those with insufficient time.

**2. Cultivating independent exercise habits:** 2018 national monitoring shows only 28.4% of 4th graders and 18.6% of 8th graders have genuine exercise habits. Eastern regions highest (32.4%, 20.7%), central regions lowest (25.7%, 16.3%). Urban students higher than rural. Longer immersive exercise time helps build habits.

**3. Local reform experiences:** Multiple provinces implemented reforms before national policy:
- Beijing (2021): daily PE class policy; 2024: 15-minute recess periods.
- Shanghai (2023): 2 hours daily exercise, 5 PE classes/week for primary, 4 for middle school.
- Yunnan (2024): 2 daily eye exercises, 30-min big recess, 15-min recess minimum.
- Tianjin (2024): morning/afternoon 30-min big recess, ensure 1 hour on + 1 hour off campus.
- Anhui (2024): daily PE class, two 30-min big recesses.
- Inner Mongolia (2025): daily PE class for compulsory education, 2/week for high school.
- Jiangsu (2025): "2•15 Special Action" — 2 hours activity, 15-min recess.
- Sichuan (2025): 2-hour requirement including PE class, recess, after-school services, and off-campus activity.

## Implementation Considerations (5 sections)

**1. Correctly understanding reform significance:** Vice Minister 王嘉毅 stated: "School sports appears to be a sports issue, but is actually a deep educational issue... 2 hours is not just a time issue, but a systematic reform that pulls one thread and moves the whole web, involving teaching, activities, competition, training, teachers, venues, evaluation, and support."

**2. Systematic structural arrangement:** 2 hours is "comprehensive" activity (can combine PE class + recess + big recess + after-school service + off-campus). Optimal structure: daily PE class + 15-min recesses + two 30-min big recesses + 1 hour after-school sports (=~3 hours on campus). Alternative: daily PE class + two 30-min big recesses + 1 hour after-school (=~2.5 hours). Requires reducing excess cultural class time, strengthening conditions, and scientific activity design.

**3. Integrated design of activity content:** 2 hours should be designed as one system connecting teaching, exercise, and competition along a time continuum, avoiding fragmented approaches. Key points: follow curriculum standards, extend classroom teaching into extracurricular activities, apply skills in daily life, and monitor/regulate exercise load across the week.

**4. Strengthening condition guarantees:** Teacher needs nearly double (e.g., PE classes increase from 4 to 5/week for grades 1-2, 3 to 5/week for grades 3-9). Solutions: expedite staffing quotas, train existing teachers as part-time PE teachers, recruit retired athletes and volunteers (e.g., Sichuan Tianfu New Area shared teacher system covering ~200 schools; Beijing #11 School with 20+ full-time and 80+ part-time PE teachers). Venue solutions: reserve space in new schools, develop "micro-playgrounds" in corners/rooftops/underground, establish venue sharing mechanisms with public facilities (e.g., Chongqing Coral Luneng Primary School's eight-theme sports park; Guizhou's corridor "micro-playgrounds").

**5. Sports injury risk prevention and handling:** Schools must not "give up eating for fear of choking" — continuing activities despite possible minor injuries. Requirements: use certified equipment, establish equipment safety ledgers, strengthen activity management (pre-activity equipment checks, decomposition of difficult movements, adequate warm-up), conduct risk training, improve insurance systems (school liability insurance, no-fault insurance, sports injury insurance, accident insurance), and use third-party mediation. 《中华人民共和国民法典》 (Civil Code) provides legal support for handling sports injury disputes.

**Conclusion:** School sports is a weak link in education power construction. Going forward, it must take comprehensive deepening of reform as its overall tone, enhancing student physical health as the overall goal, and the 2-hour comprehensive activity as the overall grip, promoting high-quality school sports development to cultivate fully-developed new-era talents.
</summary>

URL: https://www.cnaes.edu.cn/post/30435

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article by Yu Sumei and Wang Xiaoyan (China National Academy of Educational Sciences), published in *Sports Science* (2025, Issue 3), analyzes the policy requirement from the *Education Powerhouse Construction Plan (2024–2035)* mandating that primary and secondary school students engage in "no less than 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity per day" ("2-hour policy"). 

**Key Points:**

**Historical Evolution of Physical Activity Time Requirements:**
- 2007: "Ensure students exercise 1 hour daily"
- 2009 (*National Fitness Regulations*): Schools guarantee 1 hour of daily physical activity
- 2020: "1 hour each on-campus and off-campus" (later adjusted due to implementation difficulties)
- 2025: "Comprehensive physical activity time no less than 2 hours" — more flexible, emphasizing both in-school and out-of-school activities

**Value and Significance of the "2-Hour" Policy:**
1. **Promotes student physical and mental health** — addresses issues like obesity, myopia, poor stamina, and anxiety ("four small problems")
2. **Drives high-quality school sports development** — pushes for improvement in PE teacher staffing, school sports facilities, and curriculum reform

**Implementation Pathways:**

**School as the Main Channel — "Four Ones" Framework:**
- "One PE class per day" — ensure daily structured PE instruction
- "One specialty per student" — each student develops at least one sports specialty
- "One team per class" — each class forms a sports team for competitions
- "One plan per school" — tailored implementation plans reflecting school-specific conditions

**Comprehensiveness ("综合"):**
- Spatially: integrates in-class and out-of-class, on-campus and off-campus activities
- Formally: connects "learning, practice, and competition" (teaching, diligent practice, regular competition)

**Family as the Booster — "Three Things":**
- **Accompany** — parents should exercise with children
- **Supervise** — ensure completion of after-school physical activity homework
- **Guide** — provide appropriate guidance on exercise methods and intensity

**Key Challenges:**
- Insufficient professional PE teachers, especially with daily PE class requirement
- Inadequate sports facilities, with schools adopting creative solutions (renovating cafeterias, building rooftop/underground sports venues)
- Need for differentiated approaches across regions and schools

The article emphasizes that "2 hours" is not merely a time requirement but a strategic initiative to fundamentally improve student health, cultivate lifelong exercise habits, and advance high-quality school sports development through systematic school-family collaboration.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a government information notice from the Guangzhou Municipal Education Bureau, dated February 5, 2025, regarding a provincial education department directive requiring that primary and secondary school students receive no less than two hours of comprehensive physical activity per school day. The directive takes effect starting the 2025 spring semester.

Key provisions include:
- **Overall Goal**: Implement the "Education Power Construction Plan Outline (2024–2035)," uphold a "health first" educational philosophy, and ensure students get at least 2 hours of daily physical activity.
- **Target Timeline**: From the 2025 spring semester, all schools in the province must implement "Campus Sunshine Sports Activities." The Pearl River Delta region must fully implement one physical education class per day by the 2025 fall semester; the eastern, western, and northern Guangdong regions must have at least 50% of schools meeting this standard by the 2025 fall semester, with full implementation by the 2026 fall semester.
- **Specific Measures**:
  1. Increase physical activity time by adding morning/afternoon exercises (10–15 min), exploring a 15-minute recess system, and prohibiting "拖堂" (keeping students after class bell).
  2. Optimize curriculum scheduling by reducing excessive cultural subject hours and integrating one PE class per day into the timetable.
  3. Ensure facility availability through renovation, expansion, utilization of rooftop/corridor spaces, and partnerships with nearby public venues.
  4. Recruit and train sufficient PE teachers, including hiring retired athletes, veterans, retired PE teachers, and using third-party services.
  5. Establish a multi-level competition system (school, district, provincial) with at least one full-participation sports meet per semester.
- **Work Requirements**: All education departments must recognize the political and strategic importance of this policy and coordinate students' academic and physical development.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an official notice (粤教体函〔2025〕8号) issued by the Guangdong Provincial Department of Education on February 5, 2025, mandating that all primary and secondary school students in Guangdong province receive no less than 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity time on campus per day ("每天校园体育2小时"), also advancing the implementation of 1 physical education class per day.

Key requirements and goals:
- From the 2025 spring semester, all Guangdong primary and secondary schools must implement "校园阳光体育活动" (Campus Sunshine Physical Activity) with 2 hours of daily comprehensive campus physical activity.
- The Pearl River Delta region schools must fully implement 1 PE class per day from the 2025 fall semester; eastern, western, and northern Guangdong regions must reach at least 50% of schools implementing daily PE classes by fall 2025, and fully implement by fall 2026.

Specific measures include:
1. Increasing physical activity time: Using morning or after-school sessions for 10-15 minutes of varied activities, exploring morning and afternoon large-break (大课间) activities, enriching recess "micro-exercise" content, implementing a 15-minute recess system, prohibiting "拖堂" (delayed class dismissal) or restricting students' recess freedom, and coordinating PE classes, recess activities, eye exercises, morning/afternoon exercises, and after-school sports services.
2. Optimizing course scheduling: Reducing excessive academic class hours, incorporating the daily PE class into the timetable using local curriculum, school-based curriculum, and comprehensive practical activity hours.
3. Ensuring facilities: Strengthening school sports venue planning and renovation, ensuring per-student sports area meets requirements, using roofs, corridors, hallways, and other indoor space for "micro-sports fields," utilizing surrounding park green spaces, universities, communities, and public sports venues, and opening school sports venues to students during holidays.
4. Strengthening PE staffing: Using public recruitment, county-district managed school employment, teacher transfers, "walk-in teaching," hiring retired athletes and veterans, rehiring retired PE teachers, purchasing specialty course services, and cooperating with qualified third-party institutions; providing teacher training and reasonable workload arrangements.
5. Improving competition systems: Establishing province-city-county-school tiered competition systems, requiring schools to hold comprehensive sports meets or sports festivals at least once per semester, and creating a campus sports culture of "人人有项目，班班有队伍，月月有比赛" (everyone has a project, every class has a team, every month has a competition).

Work requirements: Raise political awareness, strengthen organizational leadership (including ensuring sports work funds in annual budgets), improve work systems (including safety management and emergency response plans, screening students with special constitutions or diseases unsuitable for sports), and strengthen inspection and supervision. Local plans must be submitted to the Provincial Education Department by March 1, 2025. Each school must publish its 2-hour daily campus sports schedule along with supervision phone numbers and email to parents for public oversight. Contact persons: Li Hua (体育卫生与艺术处, 020-37626353) and Chen Yanyao (基信处, 020-37628755); supervision email: lih@gdedu.gov.cn.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 3: 2025年全民健身活动状况调查统计调查制度 - 国家统计局 ---
URL: https://www.stats.gov.cn/fw/bmdcxmsp/bmzd/202506/t20250605_1960060.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an official statistical survey system document published on the website of China's National Bureau of Statistics (国家统计局) regarding the "2025 National Fitness Activity Status Survey" (2025年全民健身活动状况调查统计调查制度), dated 2025/06/05.

**Survey Purpose:** To comprehensively understand the status and characteristics of Chinese residents' physical fitness behaviors, understand residents' scientific fitness literacy, support the evaluation of the National Fitness Plan implementation, and monitor the progress of the Healthy China (健康中国) initiative.

**Survey Subjects:** Permanent residents (living locally for 6+ months) across 31 provinces (autonomous regions, municipalities), who are Chinese residents aged 3 years and above as of January 1, 2025. Subjects are divided into five age groups: 3-6, 6-9, 10-12, 13-18, and 19 years and above.

**Statistical Scope:** All 31 provinces. Each province extracts 500 districts (counties) as survey units per sampling plan; each sampled district extracts 13 villages (neighborhood committees); each village surveys 22 sample cases.

**Survey Content:** Basic national physical exercise participation including personal basic information, physical exercise behavior, and scientific fitness literacy indicators.

**Survey Methodology:** Uses stratified, multi-stage probability-proportional-to-size (PPS) sampling with household surveys. The national research group establishes the sampling frame; provincial sports departments organize work groups. In principle, the sampling frame cannot be changed by provinces; modifications require approval from the General Administration of Sport (体育总局) through provincial sports bureaus.

**Organization and Implementation:** The survey is uniformly organized by the General Administration of Sport's Mass Sports Department (群体司), with tiered implementation. Local sports management departments handle data review and reporting. The General Administration develops survey plans for the five age groups and guides provincial sports bureaus. The China Institute of Sport Science (National Physical Fitness Monitoring Center) handles specific implementation. A "2025 National Fitness Activity Status Survey Working Group" coordinates the survey, with its office at the Mass Sports Department.

**Data Publication:** Results will be published on the General Administration of Sport official website (www.sport.gov.cn) during the second half of 2025, releasing the main data on the 2025 National Fitness Activity Survey.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
调查对象：31个省（区、市）的常住人口（当地居住满6个月以上），且2025年1月1日时，满3周岁及以上的中国居民。按年龄分为3-6岁、6-9岁、10-12岁、13-18岁、19岁及以上五类人群。

--- SOURCE 4: 中小学生“每天2小时综合体育活动”如何真正落地 - 中国教育报 ---
URL: http://www.jyb.cn/rmtzcg/xwy/wzxw/202505/t20250528_2111349903.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from China Education News (published May 28, 2025) discusses the implementation of the new policy requiring primary and secondary school students to have "no less than 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity per day" (the "2 hours daily" policy), as outlined in the Education Power Building Plan (2024-2035). 

**Background and Rationale:** The policy is a response to worsening student health issues including rising rates of myopia ("small glasses"), obesity ("small chubby"), poor fitness, and mental health problems. Key statistics cited include: 51.9% of children and adolescents have myopia (2022 data); 14.8% of adolescents may have some level of depression; and student endurance, strength, and speed have been declining since 1985. Previous policies mandated "1 hour of daily physical activity" but have not achieved desired outcomes.

**Definition:** "2 hours of comprehensive physical activity" is not equivalent to 2 physical education classes. It refers to total dynamic physical activity including morning exercise, PE classes, recess activities, sports training, walking/cycling to school, and home exercise—similar to the international concept of "Physical Activity (PA)."

**Challenges:** The article identifies five main obstacles: (1) time constraints within fixed school schedules; (2) insufficient space and facilities (especially schools with less than 5 sqm per student); (3) shortage of PE teachers; (4) need for new activity content design; (5) safety concerns and liability for sports injuries.

**Proposed Solutions:** (1) Adjust class schedules (e.g., 35-minute short classes to free up time for longer recess with "micro-movement" activities); (2) use after-school services for organized sports; (3) rotate grade groups to maximize limited space; (4) distribute supervision responsibilities among all teachers, not just PE teachers; (5) establish safety insurance mechanisms.

**Implementation Model:** A suggested daily schedule: micro-movement during recess (2×8 min), sunshine sports during big recess (25-30 min), PE class (40 min), and after-school sports (30-35 min), totaling approximately 120 minutes.

**Key Success Factors:** The article emphasizes that changing school principals' mindsets is the most critical step. Parental understanding and support is also essential. It recommends phased implementation: primary schools first (1 year), then middle schools (3 years), with high schools maintaining 1 hour and piloting 2 hours where conditions permit.

**Examples:** Guangdong Huizhou Longmen County High School (2,900 students) runs morning group runs, 2 PE classes, 25-min big recess, and music-physical education classes. Chongqing Coral Luneng Primary School (4,700 students) schedules "big recess PE class" in three rotations due to space constraints and uses a "long-short class hour system" with 35-minute short classes.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"体育锻炼是增强少年儿童体质最有效的手段。现在生活条件好了，孩子们不是要吃得胖胖的，而是要长得壮壮的、练得棒棒的。体育锻炼要从小抓起，体育锻炼多一些，‘小胖墩’‘小眼镜’就少一些。" — 习近平, "治沉疴须用猛药，正是在此背景下，‘每天2小时’成为必然的选择。", "‘每天2小时’，不是要上2节体育课，而是要保障中小学生每天有不低于2小时的动态身体活动", "增加体育活动时间，施行‘每天2小时’，关键在校长。校长观念改变，是疏通堵点，打通政策落实‘最后一公里’的最重要一环。", "小课间‘微运动’（8*2=16分钟），大课间阳光运动（25—30分钟），体育课教学活动（40分钟），课后延时自主运动（30—35分钟）。总计可以基本达到甚至超过120分钟。"

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the China National Academy of Educational Sciences (CNAES) website and contains the full text of a scholarly article by Yu Sumei and Wang Xiaoyan titled "The Value Purpose and Collaborative Path of 'Primary and Secondary School Students' Daily Comprehensive Physical Activity Time Not Less Than 2 Hours'." Published in *Sports Journal* (Issue 3, 2025), the article analyzes the policy mandate from the *Education Power Building Plan (2024-2035)* requiring students to have at least 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity daily.

**Key points covered:**

1. **Historical Evolution of Physical Activity Requirements:** The policy has evolved from "1 hour daily physical activity" (2009) to "1 hour each on and off campus" (2020), and now to "at least 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity daily" (2025). 2. **Benefits of the "2 Hours" Policy:** It promotes student physical and mental health by addressing issues like obesity, poor eyesight, and weak physical fitness. It also drives high-quality school sports development by pushing for better teacher staffing and improved sports facilities.

3. **School Implementation - "Four Ones":** Schools should implement (1) One physical education class per day, (2) One specialized skill per student, (3) One sports team per class, and (4) One tailored implementation plan per school.

4. **Comprehensiveness ("Comprehensive"):** The policy emphasizes integration across spaces (in-class/out-of-class, on-campus/off-campus) and forms (learning, practice, and competition), aligned with the "Teach, Practice, Compete" framework.

5. **Family Role:** Families should support through three actions: companionship (parent-child exercise), supervision (ensuring homework completion), and guidance (proper exercise methods). The home component emphasizes diversity in physical activities.

6. **Challenges:** Issues include insufficient PE teachers, inadequate sports facilities, and misunderstandings about how to count activity time (e.g., incorrectly counting recess as physical education class time).

The article urges schools to develop individualized plans and calls for strong home-school collaboration to ensure quality implementation of the "2 hours" policy.

研究主题：影响中国中小学生每天综合体育活动时间落实的关键因素分析

需要从多个维度深入研究影响《教育强国建设规划纲要（2024—2035年）》中"每天不低于2小时"目标落实的因素：

1. 学校层面因素：
   - 体育课时安排是否充足，是否存在被文化课挤占的情况
   - 体育师资数量和质量（师生比、专职体育教师比例、专业水平）
   - 体育场地设施条件（人均体育场地面积、器材配备标准）
   - 学校体育安全管理机制和风险规避倾向
   - 校长和学校管理层对体育教育的重视程度
   - 大课间活动、课后体育服务的开展情况

2. 家庭层面因素：
   - 家长对体育教育的观念和重视程度
   - 课外辅导/作业负担对体育活动时间的挤压
   - 家庭对体育消费的投入意愿和能力
   - 家长对孩子运动安全的担忧

3. 社会层面因素：
   - 社区体育资源（公共体育设施、运动场所）的可及性
   - 社会环境对学生户外活动的安全顾虑（如交通事故、人身安全等）
   - 社会培训机构对体育教育的补充作用
   - 媒体和社会舆论对体育教育的关注度

4. 政策层面因素：
   - 中考体育考试改革对学生体育活动时间的影响
   - 学校体育工作考核评价机制（是否纳入学校评价、校长考核）
   - 教育督导对体育工作的检查力度和问责机制
   - 体育特长生招生政策的影响
   - 减负政策与体育活动时间的关系

5. 其他因素：
   - 学业压力与升学竞争对体育活动的挤出效应
   - 电子设备使用时间增加对体育活动的替代
   - 气候变化（如极端天气、雾霾等）对户外活动的影响

请引用2024-2026年的最新研究、调查报告和官方文件，优先使用中文权威来源。

--- SOURCE 1: 中共中央 国务院印发《教育强国建设规划纲要（2024－2035年）》 ---
URL: https://www.mee.gov.cn/zcwj/zyygwj/202501/t20250120_1100948.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
中共中央、国务院于2025年1月印发了《教育强国建设规划纲要（2024－2035年）》，这是一份指导中国未来教育发展的纲领性文件。纲要涵盖十大方面，主要内容包括：

**一、总体要求**：加强和改进新时代学校思想政治教育，实施新时代立德树人工程，推动大中小学思政课一体化改革创新。

**二、基础教育**：健全与人口变化相适应的基础教育资源统筹调配机制，推动义务教育优质均衡发展和城乡一体化，探索逐步扩大免费教育范围，统筹推进"双减"和教育教学质量提升。

**三、高等教育**：分类推进高校改革发展，优化高等教育布局，加快建设中国特色世界一流的大学和优势学科，有序扩大优质本科教育招生规模，扩大研究生培养规模。完善拔尖创新人才发现和培养机制，面向中小学生实施"沃土计划"，面向高中学生实施"脱颖计划"。

**四、科技与创新**：实施基础学科和交叉学科突破计划，促进青年科技人才成长发展，提高高校科技成果转化效能，建设高等研究院开辟区域发展新赛道。

**五、职业教育**：塑造多元办学、产教融合新形态，以职普融通拓宽学生成长成才通道，稳步扩大职业本科学校数量和招生规模。

**六、学习型社会与数字化**：提升终身学习公共服务水平，实施国家教育数字化战略，促进人工智能助力教育变革。

**七、教师队伍建设**：实施教育家精神铸魂强师行动，提升教师专业素质能力，提高教师政治地位、社会地位、职业地位。

**八、综合改革**：深化教育评价改革，完善人才培养与经济社会发展需要适配机制，健全教育战略性投入机制，确保国家财政性教育经费支出占GDP比例高于4%。

**九、教育对外开放**：提升全球人才培养和集聚能力，扩大国际学术交流和教育科研合作，积极参与全球教育治理。

**十、组织实施**：完善党委统一领导、党政齐抓共管的教育领导体制，营造全社会共同关心支持教育强国建设的良好环境。
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
近日，中共中央、国务院印发了《教育强国建设规划纲要（2024－2035年）》，并发出通知，要求各地区各部门结合实际认真贯彻落实。,实施新时代立德树人工程，坚持思政课建设与党的创新理论武装同步推进，加快构建以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想为核心内容的课程教材体系。,中小学生每天综合体育活动时间不低于2小时，加强校园足球建设，有效控制近视率、肥胖率。,面向中小学生实施科学素养培育"沃土计划"；面向具有创新潜质的高中学生实施"脱颖计划"等。,确保财政一般公共预算教育支出逐年只增不减，确保按在校学生人数平均的一般公共预算教育支出逐年只增不减，保证国家财政性教育经费支出占国内生产总值比例高于4%。
</key_excerpts>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This academic paper (Journal of Physical Education, Vol.32 No.2, March 2025) by Yu Sumei and Wang Xiaoyan (National Institute of Education Sciences, China) analyzes the "No Less Than 2 Hours of Comprehensive Physical Activity per Day" policy for primary and secondary school students, as outlined in the "Education Strengthening Country Planning Outline (2024-2035)." 

The paper traces the evolution of China's physical activity requirements: from "1 hour daily" (2009), to "1 hour each at school and home" (2020), to the current "2 hours of comprehensive physical activity" (2025). The "2-hour" policy aims to address student health issues ("small fat, small glasses, small bean sprouts, small anxiety") and promote school sports reform.

**Key findings:**
- The policy promotes both student physical/mental health and high-quality school sports development
- Implementation requires school-family collaboration: schools as the main channel, families as boosters
- **School-level strategy ("Four Ones"):** (1) One physical education class daily; (2) One specialty sport per student; (3) One sports team per class; (4) One customized implementation plan per school
- **Family-level strategy ("Three Things"):** Parents should provide companionship, supervision, and guidance for children's physical activities
- The "comprehensive" aspect requires integration across in-class/out-of-class, in-school/out-of-school, and the "teach, practice, compete" continuum
- Over 20 provinces have implemented 15-minute recess periods
- The policy drives improvement in sports teacher staffing and school sports facility construction
</summary>

--- SOURCE 3: 教育强国建设背景下中小学体育高质量发展对策研究 - Journals ---
URL: http://journals.viserdata.com/index.php/jscs/article/download/16939/17178

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This academic paper, published in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Science (2025, Vol. 5, No. 3), examines the high-quality development of physical education (PE) in Chinese primary and secondary schools within the context of China's goal to become an "education powerhouse" as outlined at the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China. The study uses literature review and logical analysis methods to identify three key problems: (1) lagging PE education concepts, (2) inadequate PE teacher teams (quantity, professionalism, and structure), and (3) insufficient implementation of PE activities. The paper proposes five countermeasures: (1) coordinated allocation to promote holistic student development (moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic, and labor education); (2) building high-quality, professional PE teacher teams with improved recruitment and evaluation systems; (3) implementing the policy requiring at least 2 hours of daily comprehensive physical activity for students through structured school and family-based approaches; (4) upgrading school sports facilities with modern technology, including "smart playgrounds" (as exemplified by 12 schools in Hefei) that use AI for automated performance tracking and error correction; and (5) innovating classroom teaching models by incorporating VR/AR technology and game-based learning. The paper references the "Education Powerhouse Construction Plan (2024-2035)" issued by the Central Committee of the CPC and the State Council, which mandates daily physical activity time and addresses issues like obesity (7.9% obesity rate among 6-17 year olds, up from 0.2% in 1982) and myopia among students.

4.  **Ensuring Conditions:** This requires more teachers (via recruitment, utilizing existing staff, and hiring external professionals), expanded facilities, and increased funding.
5.  **Managing Injury Risk:** Schools must implement safety protocols, proper equipment maintenance, supervision, and comprehensive insurance, while avoiding overly restrictive policies that limit physical activity.

The survey, conducted every five years since 1985, measures 24 indicators across body shape, physiological function, physical fitness, and health status.

**Key Findings:**
- **Overall improvement:** 23.8% of students aged 6–22 met the physical fitness and health standard in 2019, with a rising trend from 14.8% (2014) to 17.7% (2019) for ages 13–22. Junior high students showed the most improvement.
- **Physical development:** Height, weight, and chest circumference continued to increase across all age groups compared to 2014.
- **Lung capacity:** Increased across all age groups over the past decade, with the largest gains in junior high students.

**Contributing Factors:**
- Economic development and improved living standards.

- Family-school collaboration and health education.
- Student health awareness, sufficient daily exercise, and adequate sleep.

**Remaining Issues:**
- High rates of poor vision and myopia.
- Rising overweight and obesity rates.
- Declining grip strength.
- Declining physical fitness among university students.

**Next Steps (by the Ministry of Education):**
- Strengthen school sports programs and physical education.
- Implement school health and hygiene education policies.
- Continue comprehensive interventions for childhood myopia.
- Launch a national health school construction plan.

--- SOURCE 1: 学龄人口减少背景下我国2025—2035 年义务教育阶段体育教师 ... ---
URL: http://sdtyxyxb.magtechjournal.com/CN/PDF/10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This academic article by Shang Lipei, published in the Capital Institute of Physical Education Journal (2025, 37(5): 473-482), predicts the demand for physical education (PE) teachers in China's compulsory education stage from 2025 to 2035 against the backdrop of declining school-age population. The study uses literature review and data analysis methods.

**Background**: China's total fertility rate dropped to 1.3% in 2020, and birth numbers fell from 17.23 million in 2017 to 9.02-9.54 million in 2022-2024. School-age populations in preschool, primary, junior high, senior high, and higher education will peak in 2020, 2023, 2026, 2029, and 2032 respectively. This decline affects education resources, prompting policies like the Education Power Construction Plan (2024-2035) requiring resource allocation aligned with population changes.

**Methodology**: The study estimated enrolled student numbers (using Zhou Qin et al.'s forecasts), set PE class hours at 4.5 periods/week for primary and 3/week for junior high, calculated class numbers (2025-2028 using average class sizes of 37.97 for primary and 45.94 for junior high, decreasing by 1 person annually from 2029-2035), and used formulas: weekly PE class total = specific weekly class hours × class numbers; PE teacher demand = weekly class total ÷ teacher weekly workload.

**Key Results**:
- Primary school enrollment falls from 9,976万人 (2025) to 5,556万人 (2035); junior high from 5,481万 to 3,051万.
- **Plan A** (primary teachers at 14 hrs/week, junior high at 12 hrs/week): total demand falls from 1.1428 million (2025) to 772,500 (2035), a decrease of 37万.
- **Plan B** (primary teachers at 16 hrs/week, junior high at 14 hrs/week): total demand falls from 994,600 (2025) to 672,500 (2035), a decrease of 32万.
- Primary teacher demand: 844,500→576,600 (Plan A); 738,900→504,600 (Plan B). Junior high: 298,300→195,900 (Plan A); 255,700→167,900 (Plan B).

**Surplus/Shortage Analysis** (using linear regression projections of teacher stock based on 2010-2023 China Education Statistics Yearbook data):
- **Plan A**: Shortage and surplus coexist. From 2031, surpluses begin. Primary shortage declines from 34.44万 (2025) to 1.30万 (2030), then surplus grows from 4.04万 to 11.51万 (2031-2035). Junior high has shortage in most years through 2030 (except 2028-2029), turning to surplus of 1.75万 to 12.92万 (2031-2035).
- **Plan B**: Primary shortage declines from 23.88万 to 5.12万 (2025-2028), surplus from 2029 (1.23万 increasing to 18.71万 by 2035). Junior high already shows surplus of 4,500 in 2025, growing to 15.72万 by 2035.

**Conclusions**: (1) PE teacher demand shows a declining trend from 2025-2035 due to decreasing school-age population. (2) Storage functions for primary and junior high PE teachers were constructed. (3) Under Plan A, shortage and surplus coexist, with surplus beginning 2031. (4) Under Plan B, primary school surplus begins 2029, junior high surplus already in 2025.

**Recommendations**:
1. Strictly allocate full-time PE teachers per Ministry of Education regulations rather than increasing teacher workloads.
2. Adjust PE normal (teacher-training) student training scale based on quality and moderation principles, considering "4+3" bachelor-master pipeline programs.
3. Flexibly balance PE teacher allocation based on practical needs, addressing urban-rural and regional differences and structural vacancy issues, with cross-school/cross-level deployment.
4. Establish early warning and monitoring systems for dynamic PE teacher allocation using big data on school-age population and teacher stock.
5. Explore PE teacher exit mechanisms (e.g., early retirement programs like Ningxia's model, flexible retirement, assessment-based exit and reallocation).

The study acknowledges it is a theoretical estimate, and actual needs depend on provincial variations in class hours, class sizes, and teacher workloads.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an academic journal article published in the Journal of Capital University of Physical Education and Sports (首都体育学院学报), Vol. 37, Issue 5, 2025, pages 473-482. The article, authored by Shang Liping (尚力沛), an associate professor at the Institute of Physical Education Curriculum and Teaching, Nanjing Normal University, was received on 2025-08-28 and published on 2025-09-15. Its DOI is 10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001.

Title: "Demand Forecasting and Suggestions on the Physical Education Teachers in the Compulsory Education Stage in China from 2025 to 2035 under the Background of the Decline in School-age Population" (学龄人口减少背景下我国2025—2035年义务教育阶段体育教师需求量预测及建议).

METHODOLOGY: Using literature review and data analysis methods, the study calculates demand based on specific weekly class hours of physical education courses in primary and junior high schools and the weekly class hours of physical education teachers.

KEY FINDINGS:
1) Demand for PE teachers in the compulsory education stage will show a downward trend from 2025-2035. Under Plan A, demand ranges from 1,142,800 (2025) to 772,500 (2035) teachers. Under Plan B, demand ranges from 994,600 to 672,500.
2) Under Plan A, there is a coexistence of teacher "shortage" and "excess" - starting from 2031, the number of PE teachers will begin to show excess. Under Plan B, primary schools will see surplus starting from 2029, while junior high schools already show surplus as early as 2025.

RECOMMENDATIONS: (1) Strictly follow Ministry of Education regulations to allocate full-time PE teachers; (2) Moderately adjust the scale of PE normal student training based on quality; (3) Flexibly balance PE teacher allocation based on practical needs; (4) Implement early warning and monitoring of dynamic PE teacher allocation; (5) Explore exit mechanisms for PE teachers in the compulsory education stage.

The article includes 26 Chinese and English references, primarily covering education policy documents (e.g., 教育强国建设规划纲要 2024-2035), national population census data, and related research on teacher resource allocation. The paper is classified under G807 (Physical Education), discipline code 040303.

--- SOURCE 4: 上观新闻：6年内全球缺4400万教师，比两个中国师资还多，需年增工资1200亿美元 ---
URL: https://www.shnu.edu.cn/7c/6e/c16a818286/page.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a news article published by Shanghai Normal University's news center on November 11, 2024, republishing a report from Shangguan News (解放日报·上观新闻) by reporter Xu Ruizhe. The article covers the first Global Report on Teachers, jointly compiled by UNESCO and the International Task Force on Teachers, released at the UNESCO Teacher Education Center in Shanghai.

Key facts from the article:

**The Teacher Shortage:**
- To achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goal 4 (ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education) by 2030, the world needs 4.4 million new teachers within 6 years — more than double China's entire current teaching workforce.
- This 44 million gap is down from the 2016 projection of 69 million but still represents half of the current global teaching workforce.
- Beijing Normal University professor Zhou Zuoyu, director of UNESCO's International Research and Training Center for Rural Education, noted that China's basic education teacher workforce was 16.84 million in 2023, with 12.32 million holding bachelor's degrees and 786,800 holding graduate degrees (combined 77.86%).
- Secondary school teacher shortage (31 million) is much larger than primary school (nearly 13 million); 58% of secondary vacancies are to fill attrition, 42% are new positions.
- Sub-Saharan Africa needs 15 million new teachers by 2030 due to a growing school-age population and financial constraints. High-income countries (France, Netherlands, UK, Japan, USA) also face teacher attrition problems.

**Why the Shortage Exists:**
- Three categories of attrition factors: push factors (working conditions, teacher well-being), pull factors (salary and career development opportunities), and personal factors (retirement, health, family responsibilities).
- In half of countries, primary school teachers earn less than comparable professions. In Sub-Saharan Africa, many teachers cannot meet basic family expenses. In East/Southeast Asia, primary school teachers in Laos, Myanmar, Indonesia, and Mongolia earn an average of just $471/month (per Carlos Vargas-Tamez, head of UNESCO's Teacher Development Working Group).
- Male teachers (attrition rates 9.2% primary, 5.9% secondary) and younger teachers leave at higher rates than female teachers (4.2% primary, 5.6% secondary). Attrition follows a U-shaped curve across careers.
- Vargas-Tamez praised China/Shanghai's retired teacher program, which provides benefits comparable to local civil servants.

**How to Address the Shortage:**
- Countries need to invest approximately $120 billion annually in teacher salaries to meet universal education goals.
- Global education financing comes from governments, donors, and households; government funding accounted for 78% of global education spending in 2021, when total spending reached $5.4 trillion.
- The 2030 Education Action Framework targets allocating 4%-6% of GDP to education; the global average was 4.2% in 2021 (5% for high-income countries, only 3.1% for low-income countries in 2022). East/South Asia averaged 3.3%; China reached 4% in 2022.
- Kazakhstan doubled teacher salaries between 2020-2023 after teachers reported low pay and heavy workloads.
- Recommendations: ensure sufficient domestic public funding meeting international benchmarks of 6% of GDP and 20% of public spending; improve working conditions starting with salaries and incentives; ensure competitive compensation and gender equality in pay.

The article also includes links to the original Shangguan News article and Shanghai Normal University's "media perspectives" section. The rest of the page consists of standard Shanghai Normal University website navigation and links (portals, email, course selection, library, etc.).
</summary>

--- SOURCE 5: 乔锦忠、钟秉林等：2020—2035年我国义务教育阶段资源配置研究 ---
URL: http://www.esidea.bnu.edu.cn/zcfg/125469.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage presents a research study by Beijing Normal University scholars 乔锦忠 and 钟秉林 titled "专家观点" (Expert Opinion), published on December 22, 2021, predicting compulsory education (义务教育) school-age population changes and their impact on educational resource allocation in China during 2020-2035.

BACKGROUND AND METHODOLOGY: The study was conducted under the guidance of China's "中国教育现代化2035" (China's Education Modernization 2035) plan, which aims for quality and balanced development of compulsory education. The researchers used the Leslie matrix cohort-component method (队列要素法) and field interviews, based on sixth census data, 1% population sampling data, and recent birth data. They modeled populations by urban/rural classification, gender, and age, integrating factors including birth rates, mortality, migration, and fertility policies. The study defines compulsory education age as 6-15 years old.

KEY FINDINGS ON STUDENT NUMBERS:
1. Compulsory education student numbers will experience a short 4-year slow increase followed by an 11-year rapid decline. Student enrollment will rise from 140 million in 2020 to a peak of about 146 million in 2024, then decline to about 110 million by 2035—a drop of approximately 30 million from 2020 levels.
2. By around 2031, urban (城区) compulsory education students will exceed town (镇区) students, marking the overall transition to a city-education-dominated era. Rural students will decline to 16.23 million by 2035 (down about 10.26 million from 2020), mostly at the primary level.
3. Junior high enrollment peaks in 2029 at 50.55 million; primary school enrollment peaks in 2024 at 99.15 million.
4. Education urbanization rates exceed resident population urbanization rates (2017 rates: junior high 85.52%, primary 72.50%), so the study used enrollment-based urbanization rates rather than household registration-based rates for resource planning.

SCHOOL INFRASTRUCTURE DEMAND:
1. National compulsory education school demand declines from 2020, reaching only 140,700 schools by 2035 (down 55,200 from 2020).
2. Rural school demand drops sharply—rural primary schools decline to 35,500 by 2035 (a surplus/idle of 37,300 schools); rural junior high demand stays relatively stable at 11,400-14,200.
3. Urban areas need to build 4,000 new primary schools by 2026 (peak year) and 4,000 new junior highs by 2030 (peak year).
4. Rural teaching points (教学点) will continue declining.

TEACHER DEMAND:
Using 2019 teacher-student ratios (primary 16.85:1, junior high 12.88:1), teacher demand peaks at 9.51 million in 2025, then declines to 7.29 million by 2035. Compared with 2020, by 2035 there will be a surplus of ~1.50 million primary school teachers (~149.55万) and ~372,600 junior high teachers (37.26万). Primary school teachers peak at 5.88 million in 2024; junior high teachers peak at 3.92 million in 2029.
