SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an official notice (粤教体函〔2025〕8号) issued by the Guangdong Provincial Department of Education on February 5, 2025, mandating that all primary and secondary school students in Guangdong province receive no less than 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity time on campus per day ("每天校园体育2小时"), also advancing the implementation of 1 physical education class per day.

Key requirements and goals:
- From the 2025 spring semester, all Guangdong primary and secondary schools must implement "校园阳光体育活动" (Campus Sunshine Physical Activity) with 2 hours of daily comprehensive campus physical activity.
- The Pearl River Delta region schools must fully implement 1 PE class per day from the 2025 fall semester; eastern, western, and northern Guangdong regions must reach at least 50% of schools implementing daily PE classes by fall 2025, and fully implement by fall 2026.

Specific measures include:
1. Increasing physical activity time: Using morning or after-school sessions for 10-15 minutes of varied activities, exploring morning and afternoon large-break (大课间) activities, enriching recess "micro-exercise" content, implementing a 15-minute recess system, prohibiting "拖堂" (delayed class dismissal) or restricting students' recess freedom, and coordinating PE classes, recess activities, eye exercises, morning/afternoon exercises, and after-school sports services.
2. Optimizing course scheduling: Reducing excessive academic class hours, incorporating the daily PE class into the timetable using local curriculum, school-based curriculum, and comprehensive practical activity hours.
3. Ensuring facilities: Strengthening school sports venue planning and renovation, ensuring per-student sports area meets requirements, using roofs, corridors, hallways, and other indoor space for "micro-sports fields," utilizing surrounding park green spaces, universities, communities, and public sports venues, and opening school sports venues to students during holidays.
4. Strengthening PE staffing: Using public recruitment, county-district managed school employment, teacher transfers, "walk-in teaching," hiring retired athletes and veterans, rehiring retired PE teachers, purchasing specialty course services, and cooperating with qualified third-party institutions; providing teacher training and reasonable workload arrangements.
5. Improving competition systems: Establishing province-city-county-school tiered competition systems, requiring schools to hold comprehensive sports meets or sports festivals at least once per semester, and creating a campus sports culture of "人人有项目，班班有队伍，月月有比赛" (everyone has a project, every class has a team, every month has a competition).

Work requirements: Raise political awareness, strengthen organizational leadership (including ensuring sports work funds in annual budgets), improve work systems (including safety management and emergency response plans, screening students with special constitutions or diseases unsuitable for sports), and strengthen inspection and supervision. Local plans must be submitted to the Provincial Education Department by March 1, 2025. Each school must publish its 2-hour daily campus sports schedule along with supervision phone numbers and email to parents for public oversight. Contact persons: Li Hua (体育卫生与艺术处, 020-37626353) and Chen Yanyao (基信处, 020-37628755); supervision email: lih@gdedu.gov.cn.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 3: 2025年全民健身活动状况调查统计调查制度 - 国家统计局 ---
URL: https://www.stats.gov.cn/fw/bmdcxmsp/bmzd/202506/t20250605_1960060.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an official statistical survey system document published on the website of China's National Bureau of Statistics (国家统计局) regarding the "2025 National Fitness Activity Status Survey" (2025年全民健身活动状况调查统计调查制度), dated 2025/06/05.

**Survey Purpose:** To comprehensively understand the status and characteristics of Chinese residents' physical fitness behaviors, understand residents' scientific fitness literacy, support the evaluation of the National Fitness Plan implementation, and monitor the progress of the Healthy China (健康中国) initiative.

**Survey Subjects:** Permanent residents (living locally for 6+ months) across 31 provinces (autonomous regions, municipalities), who are Chinese residents aged 3 years and above as of January 1, 2025. Subjects are divided into five age groups: 3-6, 6-9, 10-12, 13-18, and 19 years and above.

**Statistical Scope:** All 31 provinces. Each province extracts 500 districts (counties) as survey units per sampling plan; each sampled district extracts 13 villages (neighborhood committees); each village surveys 22 sample cases.

**Survey Content:** Basic national physical exercise participation including personal basic information, physical exercise behavior, and scientific fitness literacy indicators.

**Survey Methodology:** Uses stratified, multi-stage probability-proportional-to-size (PPS) sampling with household surveys. The national research group establishes the sampling frame; provincial sports departments organize work groups. In principle, the sampling frame cannot be changed by provinces; modifications require approval from the General Administration of Sport (体育总局) through provincial sports bureaus.

**Organization and Implementation:** The survey is uniformly organized by the General Administration of Sport's Mass Sports Department (群体司), with tiered implementation. Local sports management departments handle data review and reporting. The General Administration develops survey plans for the five age groups and guides provincial sports bureaus. The China Institute of Sport Science (National Physical Fitness Monitoring Center) handles specific implementation. A "2025 National Fitness Activity Status Survey Working Group" coordinates the survey, with its office at the Mass Sports Department.

**Data Publication:** Results will be published on the General Administration of Sport official website (www.sport.gov.cn) during the second half of 2025, releasing the main data on the 2025 National Fitness Activity Survey.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
调查对象：31个省（区、市）的常住人口（当地居住满6个月以上），且2025年1月1日时，满3周岁及以上的中国居民。按年龄分为3-6岁、6-9岁、10-12岁、13-18岁、19岁及以上五类人群。

--- SOURCE 4: 中小学生“每天2小时综合体育活动”如何真正落地 - 中国教育报 ---
URL: http://www.jyb.cn/rmtzcg/xwy/wzxw/202505/t20250528_2111349903.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from China Education News (published May 28, 2025) discusses the implementation of the new policy requiring primary and secondary school students to have "no less than 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity per day" (the "2 hours daily" policy), as outlined in the Education Power Building Plan (2024-2035). 

**Background and Rationale:** The policy is a response to worsening student health issues including rising rates of myopia ("small glasses"), obesity ("small chubby"), poor fitness, and mental health problems. Key statistics cited include: 51.9% of children and adolescents have myopia (2022 data); 14.8% of adolescents may have some level of depression; and student endurance, strength, and speed have been declining since 1985. Previous policies mandated "1 hour of daily physical activity" but have not achieved desired outcomes.

**Definition:** "2 hours of comprehensive physical activity" is not equivalent to 2 physical education classes. It refers to total dynamic physical activity including morning exercise, PE classes, recess activities, sports training, walking/cycling to school, and home exercise—similar to the international concept of "Physical Activity (PA)."

**Challenges:** The article identifies five main obstacles: (1) time constraints within fixed school schedules; (2) insufficient space and facilities (especially schools with less than 5 sqm per student); (3) shortage of PE teachers; (4) need for new activity content design; (5) safety concerns and liability for sports injuries.

**Proposed Solutions:** (1) Adjust class schedules (e.g., 35-minute short classes to free up time for longer recess with "micro-movement" activities); (2) use after-school services for organized sports; (3) rotate grade groups to maximize limited space; (4) distribute supervision responsibilities among all teachers, not just PE teachers; (5) establish safety insurance mechanisms.

**Implementation Model:** A suggested daily schedule: micro-movement during recess (2×8 min), sunshine sports during big recess (25-30 min), PE class (40 min), and after-school sports (30-35 min), totaling approximately 120 minutes.

**Key Success Factors:** The article emphasizes that changing school principals' mindsets is the most critical step. Parental understanding and support is also essential. It recommends phased implementation: primary schools first (1 year), then middle schools (3 years), with high schools maintaining 1 hour and piloting 2 hours where conditions permit.

**Examples:** Guangdong Huizhou Longmen County High School (2,900 students) runs morning group runs, 2 PE classes, 25-min big recess, and music-physical education classes. Chongqing Coral Luneng Primary School (4,700 students) schedules "big recess PE class" in three rotations due to space constraints and uses a "long-short class hour system" with 35-minute short classes.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 5: 王晓燕：“中小学生每天综合体育活动时间不低于2小时”的价值 ... ---
URL: https://www.cnaes.edu.cn/post/30435

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the China National Academy of Educational Sciences (CNAES) website and contains the full text of a scholarly article by Yu Sumei and Wang Xiaoyan titled "The Value Purpose and Collaborative Path of 'Primary and Secondary School Students' Daily Comprehensive Physical Activity Time Not Less Than 2 Hours'." Published in *Sports Journal* (Issue 3, 2025), the article analyzes the policy mandate from the *Education Power Building Plan (2024-2035)* requiring students to have at least 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity daily.

**Key points covered:**

1. **Historical Evolution of Physical Activity Requirements:** The policy has evolved from "1 hour daily physical activity" (2009) to "1 hour each on and off campus" (2020), and now to "at least 2 hours of comprehensive physical activity daily" (2025). This shift reflects more practical and flexible implementation.

2. **Benefits of the "2 Hours" Policy:** It promotes student physical and mental health by addressing issues like obesity, poor eyesight, and weak physical fitness. It also drives high-quality school sports development by pushing for better teacher staffing and improved sports facilities.

3. **School Implementation - "Four Ones":** Schools should implement (1) One physical education class per day, (2) One specialized skill per student, (3) One sports team per class, and (4) One tailored implementation plan per school.

4. **Comprehensiveness ("Comprehensive"):** The policy emphasizes integration across spaces (in-class/out-of-class, on-campus/off-campus) and forms (learning, practice, and competition), aligned with the "Teach, Practice, Compete" framework.

5. **Family Role:** Families should support through three actions: companionship (parent-child exercise), supervision (ensuring homework completion), and guidance (proper exercise methods). The home component emphasizes diversity in physical activities.

6. **Challenges:** Issues include insufficient PE teachers, inadequate sports facilities, and misunderstandings about how to count activity time (e.g., incorrectly counting recess as physical education class time).

The article urges schools to develop individualized plans and calls for strong home-school collaboration to ensure quality implementation of the "2 hours" policy.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 6: 【深读】第八次全国学生体质与健康调研结果公布 ---
URL: https://m.thepaper.cn/baijiahao_14363844

SUMMARY:
<summary>
The Ministry of Education announced the results of the eighth National Student Physical Fitness and Health Survey, which is conducted every 5 years since 1985. The eighth survey was conducted in 1,258 schools across 93 cities in 31 provinces and Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, covering 374,257 students from full-time primary, secondary, and higher education institutions, measuring 24 indicators across physical form, physiological function, physical fitness, and health status.

Key findings include:
- Physical fitness excellence rate: 23.8% for students aged 6-22 in 2019, with overall rates trending upward since the 2014 National Student Physical Health Standard. The 13-22 age group's excellence rate rose from 14.8% in 2014 to 17.7% in 2019 (up 2.9 percentage points), with junior high school students showing the most improvement (up 5.1 percentage points for ages 13-15).
- Physical development: Height, weight, and chest circumference increased across all age groups for both boys and girls compared to 2014.
- Vital capacity (lung function) improved continuously over the past decade, with junior high students showing the most significant gains.
- Physical qualities (flexibility, strength, speed, endurance) improved among primary and middle school students, with notable improvements in sit-ups and running performance.
- Malnutrition decreased from 10.2% in 2019, improving by 1.6-2.6 percentage points across age groups compared to 2014.

Analysis attributes improvements to economic/social development, policy drivers, school-family collaboration, and improved health awareness. The strengthened high school entrance exam (zhongkao) physical education component has increased exercise time among middle school students—third-year junior high students (42.7%) exceeded first-year high school students (30.6%) in achieving 1 hour of daily school exercise. Campus football specialty school students had a 29.2% fitness excellence rate, higher than the 22.3% for non-specialty schools.

However, the survey identified persistent problems including high myopia/nearsightedness rates, rising overweight/obesity rates, declining grip strength, and declining university student physical fitness. The national adolescent myopia rate dropped 3.4 percentage points in 2019 compared to 2018, but rose 2.5 points in 2020 due to the pandemic (still 0.9 points below 2018 levels). Future measures include strengthening physical education classes, promoting outdoor activity and exercise, advancing university PE evaluation reform, and implementing eight special actions to reduce childhood myopia as outlined in the comprehensive myopia prevention plan.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 7: 第八次全国学生体质与健康调研显示：我国学生体质与健康状况总体改善 初中生最明显-中国教育新闻网 ---
URL: http://www.jyb.cn/rmtzcg/xwy/wzxw/202109/t20210903_617409.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
On September 3, 2021, the Chinese Ministry of Education (教育部) held a press conference announcing the results of the Eighth National Student Physical Fitness and Health Survey (第八次全国学生体质与健康调研). The survey found that the overall physical fitness and health of Chinese students has improved, with the most notable improvements among junior high school students.

Key findings from the survey:
- The national rate of students (ages 6-22) meeting physical fitness excellence standards (体质健康达标优良率) reached 23.8% in 2019.
- For students aged 13-22, the excellence rate rose from 14.8% in 2014 to 17.7% in 2019, an increase of 2.9 percentage points. By age group: students aged 13-15 rose 5.1 points, 16-18 rose 1.8 points, and 19-22 rose only 0.2 points. Junior high school students showed the greatest improvement (5.1 points), while university students improved the least.
- Physical development indicators (height, weight, chest circumference) continued to improve across all age groups.
- Lung capacity levels rose overall over the past 10 years, with the most significant gains among junior high students.
- Flexibility, strength, speed, and endurance improved for primary and junior high students but showed no significant improvement among university students.

Policy factors driving improvements (per the Ministry's official):

# 中国学生体质与健康调研报告. 中国学生体质与健康调研报告5一调研背景与目的随着我国社会经济的快速发展和教育改革的不断深入，学生的健康问题日益受到广泛关注。近年来，我国学生体质健康水平总体呈现下降趋势，特别是城市学生肥胖近视等健康问题突出，农村学生体质健康水平相对滞后。为全面了解我国学生体质健康状况，分析存在的问题，为制定相关政策提供科学依据，本研究开展了全国学生体质与健康调研。本次调研旨在全面掌握我国学生体质健康状况分析影响学生体质健康的主要因素，提出改善学生体质健康的对策建议。当前，我国学生体质健康问题已经成为影响青少年健康成长的重要因素。首先，学生课业负担过重，导致体育锻炼时间不足，影响了学生的身体素质。其次，随着生活水平的提高，学生膳食结构不合理，营养过剩和营养不足并存，影响了学生的生长发育。此外，随着电子产品普及学生户外活动时间减少，视力问题日益严重。为了解决这些问题，有必要开展一次全国性的学生体质与健康调研.

--- SOURCE 1: 学龄人口减少背景下我国2025—2035年义务教育阶段体育教师 ... ---
URL: http://sdtyxyxb.magtechjournal.com/CN/10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage presents the academic article "Demand Forecasting and Suggestions on the Physical Education Teachers in the Compulsory Education Stage in China from 2025 to 2035 under the Background of the Decline in School-age Population" (学龄人口减少背景下我国2025—2035年义务教育阶段体育教师需求量预测及建议), authored by SHANG Lipei (尚力沛), Associate Professor at the Institute of Physical Education Curriculum and Teaching, Nanjing Normal University. The article was published in the Journal of Capital University of Physical Education and Sports (首都体育学院学报), 2025, Vol. 37, Issue 5, pages 473-482, with DOI: 10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001. It was received on 2025-08-28 and published online on 2025-11-06.

METHODOLOGY: The study uses literature review and data analysis methods, calculating demand based on specific weekly class hours for physical education in primary and junior high schools combined with weekly class hours per PE teacher.

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Demand for PE teachers in compulsory education will show a downward trend from 2025 to 2035 due to declining school-age population.
2. Under Plan A: demand ranges from 1.1428 million (2025) down to 772,500 (2035) teachers.
3. Under Plan B: demand ranges from 994,600 (2025) down to 672,500 (2035) teachers.
4. Under Plan A, both shortage and excess coexist, with excess beginning in 2031.
5. Under Plan B, primary schools begin to show surplus starting in 2029, while junior high schools already show surplus starting in 2025.

RECOMMENDATIONS for PE teacher allocation: strictly follow Ministry of Education regulations to allocate full-time PE teachers; moderately adjust the scale of PE teacher training based on quality; flexibly balance PE teacher allocation based on practical needs; implement early warning and monitoring of dynamic teacher allocation; and explore exit mechanisms for compulsory education PE teachers.

The article includes 26 references in Chinese, covering topics such as the 7th National Population Census data, the Education Power Nation Construction Plan (2024-2035), national education statistics, and prior studies on teacher resource allocation. Classification: G807 (Physical Education).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"The demand for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage will show a downward trend as the years go by from 2025 to 2035. Based on the total Plan A, the demand range for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage in China from 2025 to 2035 is between 1.1428 million and 772,500." "Based on the combined Plan B, the demand range for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage in China from 2025 to 2035 is between 994,600 and 672,500." "Starting from 2031, the number of physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage will begin to show an excess." "Surplus will occur in primary schools starting from 2029, and in junior high schools, it has already occurred in 2025." "The suggestions for the allocation of physical education teachers in China's compulsory education stage in the next stage are as follows: Strictly follow the relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education to allocate full-time physical education teachers, moderately adjust the scale of physical education normal student training based on quality, flexibly balance the allocation of physical education teachers based on practical needs, do a good job in early warning and monitoring the dynamic allocation of physical education teachers in compulsory education, and explore the exit methods for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage."
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 教育部关于加强新时代中小学体育教师队伍建设若干举措的通知 - 中华人民共和国教育部政府门户网站 ---
URL: http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A10/s3735/202501/t20250124_1176809.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an official notice published by China's Ministry of Education (中华人民共和国教育部) on January 24, 2025 (issued January 17, 2025), titled "Notice on Several Measures to Strengthen the Building of Physical Education Teaching Staff in Primary and Secondary Schools in the New Era" (教育部关于加强新时代中小学体育教师队伍建设若干举措的通知), document number 教师〔2025〕1号 (Teacher [2025] No. 1).

The notice outlines ten key measures to build a strong PE teacher workforce for primary and secondary schools:

1. **Clear goals**: By 2027, improve the quantity and structure of PE teacher teams with better teaching quality; by 2035, form a comprehensive mechanism aligned with education modernization and building an education powerhouse.

2. **Strict ethics**: Incorporate educator spirit and Chinese sports spirit into PE teacher training; enforce strict standards for professional ethics with "zero tolerance" for violations.

3. **Increase training**: Expand PE education major enrollment in free teacher education programs and "Excellent Teacher Plan"; strengthen practical training; encourage universities to offer PE micro-majors for non-PE students.

4. **Optimize recruitment**: Set PE teacher staffing standards at no higher than a teacher-student ratio of 5:1 for primary schools, 6:1 for junior high, and 8:1 for senior high; recruit excellent retired athletes (especially football players) and veterans; require second-level athlete certificates for non-PE majors.

5. **Coordinate resources**: Establish monitoring mechanisms, promote "county-managed, school-employed" reform, teacher rotation, cross-school teaching, and township walk-in teaching for rural small schools.

6. **Enhance capabilities**: Establish training bases, optimize the "National Training Plan," focus on football, basketball, volleyball, and traditional Chinese sports training; implement AI-empowered education to boost digital literacy.

7. **Implement coach positions**: Each county should set at least one full-time coach position; recruit retired athletes with first-level athlete certification; allow mutual job transfers between coaches and PE teachers with proper qualifications.

8. **Improve evaluation and incentives**: Count PE teachers' work in recess activities, fitness monitoring, after-school training, competitions, and walk-in teaching toward workload; ensure equal treatment in titles, benefits, and awards as other subjects; guarantee a certain proportion of PE teachers in teaching awards.

9. **Strengthen organizational leadership**: Include PE teacher team building in the supervision and evaluation of county compulsory education quality; strengthen full-time PE teaching researcher teams.

10. **Ensure funding**: Increase school sports funding, include PE work costs in annual budgets, and guide social funds to support primary and secondary school sports.

The notice was published on the Ministry of Education's official website (www.moe.gov.cn) on January 24, 2025.
</summary>

- Eligibility: Must have teaching certificates and meet legal requirements (Teacher Law, Teacher Qualification Regulations); generally requires bachelor's degree or above, mainly normal (teacher-training) majors; age not exceeding 32 years (veterans and retired athletes may have relaxed age limits with consideration for service years); no criminal records. Preference for Western Plan volunteers, those with teaching experience, and normal graduates with 6+ months of teaching internship. Outgoing teachers should be placed in shortage subjects like moral/legal education, physical education, foreign languages, science, labor, arts, information technology, mental health, and special education.

WORK REQUIREMENTS:
1. Recruitment: Hiring must be completed by end of July 2025; exams should test professional and teaching competency; remote hardship areas may lower/waive exam ratios or use interviews/direct assessment; encourages high-level universities ("双一流") to send outstanding graduates.
2. Training: Comprehensive training programs aligned with education-power building goals; integrate educator spirit and teacher ethics; strengthen pre/post-service training and skills training for non-normal program teachers; encourage inclusion in local master teacher studios.
3. Management: Three-year service period teachers who pass assessment and choose to stay must be promptly placed into permanent establishment (入编) with continuous service/seniority calculation, no probation period; data maintained in the National Teacher Management Information System (also used for postgrad exam score bonus eligibility).
4. Compensation: Central government salary subsidy: 41,800 yuan/person/year in western regions; 38,800 yuan/person/year in central regions; salaries must be paid on time with social insurance; equal treatment with local public school in-service teachers in pay, professional title evaluation, honors, and annual assessment; implement post-service preferential policies and provide temporary housing.
5. Guidance/Deadline: Localities must submit 2026 plan county/school/position proposals via the National Teacher Management Information System by December 31, 2025.

URL: http://sdtyxyxb.magtechjournal.com/CN/10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage presents the academic article "Demand Forecasting and Suggestions on the Physical Education Teachers in the Compulsory Education Stage in China from 2025 to 2035 under the Background of the Decline in School-age Population" (学龄人口减少背景下我国2025—2035年义务教育阶段体育教师需求量预测及建议), authored by SHANG Lipei (尚力沛), Associate Professor at the Institute of Physical Education Curriculum and Teaching, Nanjing Normal University. The article was published in the Journal of Capital University of Physical Education and Sports (首都体育学院学报), 2025, Vol. 37, Issue 5, pages 473-482, with DOI: 10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001. It was received on 2025-08-28 and published online on 2025-11-06.

METHODOLOGY: The study uses literature review and data analysis methods, calculating demand based on specific weekly class hours for physical education in primary and junior high schools combined with weekly class hours per PE teacher.

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Demand for PE teachers in compulsory education will show a downward trend from 2025 to 2035 due to declining school-age population.
2. Under Plan A: demand ranges from 1.1428 million (2025) down to 772,500 (2035) teachers.
3. Under Plan B: demand ranges from 994,600 (2025) down to 672,500 (2035) teachers.
4. Under Plan A, both shortage and excess coexist, with excess beginning in 2031.
5. Under Plan B, primary schools begin to show surplus starting in 2029, while junior high schools already show surplus starting in 2025.

RECOMMENDATIONS for PE teacher allocation: strictly follow Ministry of Education regulations to allocate full-time PE teachers; moderately adjust the scale of PE teacher training based on quality; flexibly balance PE teacher allocation based on practical needs; implement early warning and monitoring of dynamic teacher allocation; and explore exit mechanisms for compulsory education PE teachers.

The article includes 26 references in Chinese, covering topics such as the 7th National Population Census data, the Education Power Nation Construction Plan (2024-2035), national education statistics, and prior studies on teacher resource allocation. Classification: G807 (Physical Education).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"The demand for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage will show a downward trend as the years go by from 2025 to 2035. Based on the total Plan A, the demand range for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage in China from 2025 to 2035 is between 1.1428 million and 772,500." "Based on the combined Plan B, the demand range for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage in China from 2025 to 2035 is between 994,600 and 672,500." "Starting from 2031, the number of physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage will begin to show an excess." "Surplus will occur in primary schools starting from 2029, and in junior high schools, it has already occurred in 2025." "The suggestions for the allocation of physical education teachers in China's compulsory education stage in the next stage are as follows: Strictly follow the relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education to allocate full-time physical education teachers, moderately adjust the scale of physical education normal student training based on quality, flexibly balance the allocation of physical education teachers based on practical needs, do a good job in early warning and monitoring the dynamic allocation of physical education teachers in compulsory education, and explore the exit methods for physical education teachers in the compulsory education stage."

This is an official notice (教师厅〔2025〕1号) jointly issued by the General Offices of China's Ministry of Education and Ministry of Finance (dated May 8, 2025) regarding the implementation of the 2025 "Special Post Plan" (特岗计划) for rural compulsory education school teachers.

KEY POLICY POINTS:
- Scope: Covers former contiguous special hardship areas, national/provincial poverty-alleviation key counties in central/western China, western "两基" counties, minority autonomous prefectures in central provinces under western development, and special-needs border/minority counties.
- Recruitment quota: 20,976 teachers nationwide in 2025 (detailed quotas per province in attached allocation table).
- Eligibility: Must have teaching certificates and meet legal requirements (Teacher Law, Teacher Qualification Regulations); generally requires bachelor's degree or above, mainly normal (teacher-training) majors; age not exceeding 32 years (veterans and retired athletes may have relaxed age limits with consideration for service years); no criminal records. Preference for Western Plan volunteers, those with teaching experience, and normal graduates with 6+ months of teaching internship. Outgoing teachers should be placed in shortage subjects like moral/legal education, physical education, foreign languages, science, labor, arts, information technology, mental health, and special education.

2. Training: Comprehensive training programs aligned with education-power building goals; integrate educator spirit and teacher ethics; strengthen pre/post-service training and skills training for non-normal program teachers; encourage inclusion in local master teacher studios.

5. Guidance/Deadline: Localities must submit 2026 plan county/school/position proposals via the National Teacher Management Information System by December 31, 2025.

--- SOURCE 3: 以“本土经验”应对世界级难题 - 新华网客户端 ---
URL: https://app.xinhuanet.com/news/article.html?articleId=202607178b6beecf73d642eda9e8230058666596

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article (published July 17, 2026, by 半月谈/Xinhua's Banyuetan, written by 魏靖宇) examines how China has developed uniquely "local experiences" (本土经验) to tackle world-class challenges in basic education, rather than copying Western models. These challenges include managing a vast and diverse system, significant urban-rural gaps, and structural teacher shortages.

**Key problems and scale:** China has 430,000 primary/secondary schools and kindergartens with 220 million students, including 157 million in compulsory education. High school age population is expected to keep growing, requiring expansion of school capacity.

**Strategy 1 - Solving large-scale governance through "national unified standards + provincial coordination":** The National Ministry of Education (department head 田祖荫) emphasizes a "bottom-line" approach with rigid minimum requirements for school buildings, equipment, and staffing. The central government sets standards and policies; provincial levels coordinate finances, staffing, and teachers to overcome uneven county finances; county levels focus on implementation, district management, nearby enrollment, and teacher rotation. A four-tier (national/provincial/municipal/county) education quality monitoring system strengthens local government accountability. Example given: Chongqing's rural schools, like 岑龙小学 in Xiushan County, were transformed through special funding projects.

**Strategy 2 - Narrowing urban-rural gaps through "urban-rural integration + resource sinking":** Measures include urban-rural school community building, district management, and group-run schooling. By end of 2025, all 2,895 counties achieved basic balanced compulsory education, with 572 achieving high-quality balance. The "County High School Revitalization Action Plan" was issued in September 2025 (county high schools serve ~60% of China's high school students). Some regions are experimenting with "city-county combined" management reforms (e.g., Ordos, Inner Mongolia) to shift from "county-level small circulation" to "municipal-level large coordination," sharing teachers, resources, and unified teaching with bundled assessment.

**Strategy 3 - Addressing structural teacher shortages:** China has ~16 million full-time basic education teachers (2025). Structural imbalances exist—potential oversupply of primary teachers due to declining student numbers, but shortages in high school/immigrant-inflow areas, and shortages of arts, PE, music, science teachers in rural/weak schools. Solutions include the 特岗计划 (Special Post Plan), 优师计划 (Excellent Teacher Plan), and 银龄讲学 (Silver Age program) for targeted rural and western region training. Example: 120 retired teachers from Zhejiang taught in Aba Prefecture, Sichuan in fall 2025. Digital tools: the "National Smart Education Public Service Platform" is the world's largest national education resource library, used with dedicated classrooms (专递课堂), famous teacher classrooms, and network classrooms to alleviate rural teacher shortages (e.g., a distance physics class in Siziwang Banner, Inner Mongolia, taught from Beijing 101 Middle School).

**Expert quotes:** Professor 张志勇 (Beijing Normal University) notes China's joint teaching research (联合教研) system is listed among the "top five globally learnable experiences," reinforcing teachers' community awareness and ensuring curriculum policy implementation. OECD surveys confirm this. Professor 李政涛 (East China Normal University) emphasizes resources' flow to weaker areas through pairing and co-construction.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a news article from 科技日报 (Science and Technology Daily) reporting on the release of the "2025 Annual Report on Digital Literacy of Primary and Secondary School Teachers in China" (《2025年中国中小学教师数字素养年度报告》). The report was released on May 12 at the 2026 World Digital Education Conference, during the parallel session "Preparing Teachers for Future Schools."

Key findings from the report, which surveyed 530,000 primary and secondary school teachers across 19 provinces/regions:

1. AI adoption in education: 
- 14.77% of teachers use AI tools daily; only 3.41% have never used them
- 85.17% believe AI helps expand teaching resources; 81.00% say AI saves lesson preparation time
- Most popular tools: AI tools built into smart teaching platforms (82.68%) and general large language models (76.20%)

2. Application depth: Most teachers are in early/exploratory stages:
- About one-third use AI for shallow assistance (searching information, generating simple materials)
- Another ~30% use AI purposefully in specific teaching segments
- Less than 20% integrate AI throughout the entire teaching process
- Only about 10% use AI to innovate teaching models
- Current common uses: generating teaching resources, assisting classroom interaction; less used for grading assignments or administrative tasks

3. Urban-rural gap narrowing (a highlight of the report):
- Urban and rural teachers show basically convergent performance on technological value understanding, resource usage willingness, and practical will
- 13 indicators show differences within 5%
- Over 90% of teachers in eastern regions hold positive attitudes toward AI; over 70% in central and western regions

4. Training needs: Most teachers want practical guidance on resource development, basic operations, and scenario applications; eastern teachers desire advanced training in data analysis and intelligent agent development

5. Ethical concerns: Top three concerns are student over-dependence on AI, data privacy leakage, and information misinformation; nearly half of teachers call for AI application regulations and ethical guidelines

Recommendations: Build a step-by-step development path from basic operation to innovative leadership; implement differentiated strategies (eastern regions explore deep AI-teaching integration, central/western regions rely on the National Smart Education Platform for precise resource delivery); establish cross-regional teaching research communities.

The assessment was based on the "Teacher Digital Literacy" education industry standard, covering five dimensions: digital awareness, digital technology knowledge and skills, digital application, digital social responsibility, and professional development. It marked the first time an "AI + Education" application perspective was included.

--- SOURCE 5: Kellogg Insight - 农村和城市社区之间存在着教育差距，技术是否能弥补这种差距？ ---
URL: https://insight.kellogg.northwestern.edu/zh/article/education-gap-distance-learning

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Kellogg School of Management research article (published March 1, 2021) examining whether technology can bridge the education gap between rural and urban communities, based on research by Nicola Bianchi (Kellogg assistant professor of strategy), Yi Lu (Tsinghua University), and Hong Song (Fudan University). 

The background: A 2015 OECD standardized assessment of 37 countries found that 15-year-old students in urban schools outperform rural students by roughly one full year of schooling, even accounting for socioeconomic background. In China, the gap was particularly stark—as of 2000, only 14% of rural middle school teachers held bachelor's degrees (less than half the urban rate), and only 7% of rural students continued to high school compared to urban students at a rate nine times higher.

In 2004, the Chinese government launched a four-year program to close this gap by connecting over 100 million rural students to high-quality urban teachers via satellite, internet, and CD recordings—arguably the largest educational technology intervention in world history. Rural students watched recorded lectures by top urban teachers approximately seven times per week, each about 45 minutes, in school classrooms under local teacher supervision.

Key findings from analysis of 2014 China Family Panel Studies data (respondents asked where they lived at age 12, enabling researchers to identify program exposure):
- Rural students exposed to the program completed 0.85 more years of schooling than peers
- About ten years after middle school, these students earned 59% more than same-county peers not reached by the reform
- Students moved away from farming (the most common rural job) toward jobs requiring cognitive skills
- The program closed 21% of the existing urban-rural education gap and 78% of the income gap
- Recorded lectures by highly qualified teachers had the most significant impact; "no data or examples corroborate" that other technologies provided significant benefits

Important caveat from Bianchi: the positive results may not translate to pandemic-era remote learning, because China's reform placed students in a supervised classroom environment, unlike most students learning at home today. He notes that while many industries may adopt remote models post-pandemic, education is unlikely to be among them given the benefits of in-person learning—though technology can still help rural areas obtain things even in-person teaching cannot provide.

The working paper is titled "The Effects of Computer-Assisted Learning on Students' Long-Term Development" (2020), authored by Bianchi, Yi Lu, and Hong Song.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"技术可以是一种由国内最优秀教师将高质量的教育带到农村地区、而不必试图说服教师搬迁的绝佳方式。毕安奇说道。换言之，在提高这些服务不足地区的教育质量上，技术可以成为我们实现这个目标的渠道。" , "有机会接受政府计算机辅助学习计划的农村学生与没有接受该计划的学生相比，多完成了0.85年的学校教育。值得注意的是，在接受初中教育的大约十年后，这些农村学生的收入也比改革未触及的同县同龄人多出59%。", "有趣的是不仅收入增加，职业类型也有差别。毕安奇说道。接触教育技术让这些学生逃脱中国农村地区最常见的工作，也就是务农。他们离开这类工作，奔赴更注重认知技能的工作。", "我们一般提到远程学习时，我们想到的是学生自己在家上课或听课，而且有时没有任何形式的监督。毕安奇说。中国的例子很不一样，因为学生是在课堂上课，并且由当地的老师直接监督。"

URL: https://jyj.gz.gov.cn/gkmlpt/content/10/10105/post_10105071.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a government information notice from the Guangzhou Municipal Education Bureau, dated February 5, 2025, regarding a provincial education department directive requiring that primary and secondary school students receive no less than two hours of comprehensive physical activity per school day. The directive takes effect starting the 2025 spring semester.

Key provisions include:
- **Overall Goal**: Implement the "Education Power Construction Plan Outline (2024–2035)," uphold a "health first" educational philosophy, and ensure students get at least 2 hours of daily physical activity.
- **Target Timeline**: From the 2025 spring semester, all schools in the province must implement "Campus Sunshine Sports Activities." The Pearl River Delta region must fully implement one physical education class per day by the 2025 fall semester; the eastern, western, and northern Guangdong regions must have at least 50% of schools meeting this standard by the 2025 fall semester, with full implementation by the 2026 fall semester.
- **Specific Measures**:
  1. Increase physical activity time by adding morning/afternoon exercises (10–15 min), exploring a 15-minute recess system, and prohibiting "拖堂" (keeping students after class bell).
  2. Optimize curriculum scheduling by reducing excessive cultural subject hours and integrating one PE class per day into the timetable.
  3. Ensure facility availability through renovation, expansion, utilization of rooftop/corridor spaces, and partnerships with nearby public venues.

## Policy Background (3 sections)

**1. Evolution of daily physical activity time policy (5 stages):**
- Stage 1 (1950s): 1951 State Council decision restricted student activities, recommending 1-1.5 hours of daily physical/recreational activity due to excessive academic workloads threatening health.
- Stage 2 (1978-1990s): After Cultural Revolution, 1978 notice required average 1 hour daily organized exercise; 1990 《学校体育工作条例》 legally mandated 1 hour daily physical activity (including PE classes).
- Stage 3 (2005-2011): Multiple documents (2005, 2006, 2007, 2009 《全民健身条例》, 2011 Government Work Report) clarified that the 1 hour must be on-campus time.
- Stage 4 (2020-present): Shift to requirement of 2 hours daily comprehensive activity (can be on or off campus).
- Stage 5: The 2-hour requirement targeting primary and secondary students (not university students).

**Key policy milestones for the 2-hour requirement:**
- October 2020: 中办国办 document first mentioned ensuring 2 hours daily (1 hour on campus + 1 hour off campus).
- Early 2024: Ministry of Education included "2-hour daily exercise pilot for compulsory education students" in annual work priorities.
- September 26, 2024: Vice Minister of Education 王嘉毅 announced the 2-hour requirement (one PE class daily + 1 hour after-class exercise).
- December 27, 2024: MOE held national school sports reform symposium in Anhui.
- January 2025: 《教育强国建设规划纲要(2024—2035年)》 formally required "中小学生每天综合体育活动时间不低于2小时".

**2. School sports as key content of education power construction:** School sports has political character (part of five-fold education), people's character (affects family well-being), and strategic character (national talent competition). Countries like US, UK, Finland, Australia, Japan are all strengthening school sports.

**3. New education ecosystem creating conditions:** Education structure reform, quality improvements (91.1% preschool enrollment, 95.7% nine-year compulsory education completion, 60.2% higher education enrollment), and "double reduction" policy (双减) freeing up student time. 92.7% of schools conduct arts/sports activities; 90%+ of students voluntarily participate in after-school services.

## Practical Basis (3 sections)

**1. Addressing chronic weakness in student physical fitness:** Despite 4 high-level policy documents over ~40 years (2007, 2012, 2016, 2020), student fitness hasn't fundamentally improved. 2023 national tests showed: 87.1% pass rate (down 2.9 percentage points from 2021), 35.3% excellent rate (down 3.3 points), 12.9% fail rate. Chongqing survey: 64.1% of students exercise less than 1 hour after school; nearly 60% exercise less than 30 minutes daily. Students with 1+ hour daily exercise had 27.4% excellent fitness rate vs 17.7% for those with insufficient time.

**2. Cultivating independent exercise habits:** 2018 national monitoring shows only 28.4% of 4th graders and 18.6% of 8th graders have genuine exercise habits. Eastern regions highest (32.4%, 20.7%), central regions lowest (25.7%, 16.3%). Urban students higher than rural. Longer immersive exercise time helps build habits.

**3. Local reform experiences:** Multiple provinces implemented reforms before national policy:
- Beijing (2021): daily PE class policy; 2024: 15-minute recess periods.
- Shanghai (2023): 2 hours daily exercise, 5 PE classes/week for primary, 4 for middle school.
- Yunnan (2024): 2 daily eye exercises, 30-min big recess, 15-min recess minimum.
- Tianjin (2024): morning/afternoon 30-min big recess, ensure 1 hour on + 1 hour off campus.
- Anhui (2024): daily PE class, two 30-min big recesses.
- Inner Mongolia (2025): daily PE class for compulsory education, 2/week for high school.
- Jiangsu (2025): "2•15 Special Action" — 2 hours activity, 15-min recess.
- Sichuan (2025): 2-hour requirement including PE class, recess, after-school services, and off-campus activity.

## Implementation Considerations (5 sections)

**1. Correctly understanding reform significance:** Vice Minister 王嘉毅 stated: "School sports appears to be a sports issue, but is actually a deep educational issue... 2 hours is not just a time issue, but a systematic reform that pulls one thread and moves the whole web, involving teaching, activities, competition, training, teachers, venues, evaluation, and support."

**2. Systematic structural arrangement:** 2 hours is "comprehensive" activity (can combine PE class + recess + big recess + after-school service + off-campus). Optimal structure: daily PE class + 15-min recesses + two 30-min big recesses + 1 hour after-school sports (=~3 hours on campus). Alternative: daily PE class + two 30-min big recesses + 1 hour after-school (=~2.5 hours). Requires reducing excess cultural class time, strengthening conditions, and scientific activity design.

**3. Integrated design of activity content:** 2 hours should be designed as one system connecting teaching, exercise, and competition along a time continuum, avoiding fragmented approaches. Key points: follow curriculum standards, extend classroom teaching into extracurricular activities, apply skills in daily life, and monitor/regulate exercise load across the week.

**4. Strengthening condition guarantees:** Teacher needs nearly double (e.g., PE classes increase from 4 to 5/week for grades 1-2, 3 to 5/week for grades 3-9). Solutions: expedite staffing quotas, train existing teachers as part-time PE teachers, recruit retired athletes and volunteers (e.g., Sichuan Tianfu New Area shared teacher system covering ~200 schools; Beijing #11 School with 20+ full-time and 80+ part-time PE teachers). Venue solutions: reserve space in new schools, develop "micro-playgrounds" in corners/rooftops/underground, establish venue sharing mechanisms with public facilities (e.g., Chongqing Coral Luneng Primary School's eight-theme sports park; Guizhou's corridor "micro-playgrounds").

**5. Sports injury risk prevention and handling:** Schools must not "give up eating for fear of choking" — continuing activities despite possible minor injuries. Requirements: use certified equipment, establish equipment safety ledgers, strengthen activity management (pre-activity equipment checks, decomposition of difficult movements, adequate warm-up), conduct risk training, improve insurance systems (school liability insurance, no-fault insurance, sports injury insurance, accident insurance), and use third-party mediation. 《中华人民共和国民法典》 (Civil Code) provides legal support for handling sports injury disputes.

**Conclusion:** School sports is a weak link in education power construction. Going forward, it must take comprehensive deepening of reform as its overall tone, enhancing student physical health as the overall goal, and the 2-hour comprehensive activity as the overall grip, promoting high-quality school sports development to cultivate fully-developed new-era talents.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage presents the academic article "Demand Forecasting and Suggestions on the Physical Education Teachers in the Compulsory Education Stage in China from 2025 to 2035 under the Background of the Decline in School-age Population" (学龄人口减少背景下我国2025—2035年义务教育阶段体育教师需求量预测及建议), authored by SHANG Lipei (尚力沛), Associate Professor at the Institute of Physical Education Curriculum and Teaching, Nanjing Normal University. The article was published in the Journal of Capital University of Physical Education and Sports (首都体育学院学报), 2025, Vol. 37, Issue 5, pages 473-482, with DOI: 10.14036/j.cnki.cn11-4513.2025.05.001. It was received on 2025-08-28 and published online on 2025-11-06.

METHODOLOGY: The study uses literature review and data analysis methods, calculating demand based on specific weekly class hours for physical education in primary and junior high schools combined with weekly class hours per PE teacher.

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Demand for PE teachers in compulsory education will show a downward trend from 2025 to 2035 due to declining school-age population.
2. Under Plan A: demand ranges from 1.1428 million (2025) down to 772,500 (2035) teachers.
3. Under Plan B: demand ranges from 994,600 (2025) down to 672,500 (2035) teachers.
4. Under Plan A, both shortage and excess coexist, with excess beginning in 2031.
5. Under Plan B, primary schools begin to show surplus starting in 2029, while junior high schools already show surplus starting in 2025.

RECOMMENDATIONS for PE teacher allocation: strictly follow Ministry of Education regulations to allocate full-time PE teachers; moderately adjust the scale of PE teacher training based on quality; flexibly balance PE teacher allocation based on practical needs; implement early warning and monitoring of dynamic teacher allocation; and explore exit mechanisms for compulsory education PE teachers.

The article includes 26 references in Chinese, covering topics such as the 7th National Population Census data, the Education Power Nation Construction Plan (2024-2035), national education statistics, and prior studies on teacher resource allocation. Classification: G807 (Physical Education).
</summary>

--- SOURCE 2: 2023见顶、2026承压：人口曲线与教师编制 ---
URL: https://www.eol.cn/news/guancha/202509/t20250915_2689958.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Chinese educational news article from 教育在线 (China Education Online) published on 2025-09-15, analyzing how China's declining birth rate is impacting teacher staffing and school resources in compulsory education (primary and middle schools).

**Key Points:**
- The article highlights the stark contrast between overcrowded middle schools and emptying primary schools due to shifting demographics.
- In Heze City, Shandong Province, the 22nd Middle School in Peony District admitted 94 classes of new first-year middle school students in 2025, sparking public concern about quality. Meanwhile, in Hengshan County, Hunan, a primary school's 6th grade had 43 students while 1st grade had only 2; the county's education bureau announced in August that 90 elementary school teachers would be reassigned to non-educational institutions.
- Multiple provinces (Fujian, Jiangxi, Hubei) are selecting primary school teachers to transfer to middle schools. Ezhou, Hubei reduced 500 elementary teacher positions to reallocate to middle schools.

**Key Data:**
- 2024 national data: Primary school enrollment fell sharply to 16.1616 million (−2.6125 million year-over-year), while middle school enrollment rose to 18.4875 million (+941,200).
- Primary school population peaked in 2023; middle school population will peak in 2026 and then decline.
- National school-age population projected to fall from 328 million (2021) to ~250 million by 2035, shifting from a spindle shape to an inverted pyramid structure.
- Southwest University projections: Primary teacher demand peaked in 2023-2024 (~6.86 million) and will decline; middle school teacher demand peaks in 2026 (~4.6 million).
- 2026-2030: Primary teacher demand to decrease by 1.47 million (820,000 retirements, 650,000 surplus); middle school demand decreases by 250,000 but faces a 330,000 shortfall due to 580,000 retirements.
- 2031-2035: Primary teachers to decrease by another 390,000; middle school teachers decrease by 1.5 million (680,000 retirements, 820,000 surplus).

**Policy Solutions:**
- Zhejiang (2017-2019): Adjusted staffing for 5,786 schools and 5,961 posts, reducing 4,841 positions and transferring 3,467 across school levels via "county-managed school employment" (县管校聘).
- Changzhou, Jiangsu: 6,680 teachers participated in exchange rotations during the 14th Five-Year Plan period, including 3,371 backbone teachers.

The article concludes that teacher resource allocation must adapt structurally to population changes, requiring flexible cross-segment and cross-region adjustment mechanisms, with the key being "strengthening teachers" for national strength while maintaining quality as numbers decline.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 3: 教育部关于加强新时代中小学体育教师队伍建设若干举措的通知 - 中华人民共和国教育部政府门户网站 ---
URL: http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A10/s3735/202501/t20250124_1176809.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an official notice published by China's Ministry of Education (中华人民共和国教育部) on January 24, 2025 (issued January 17, 2025), titled "Notice on Several Measures to Strengthen the Building of Physical Education Teaching Staff in Primary and Secondary Schools in the New Era" (教育部关于加强新时代中小学体育教师队伍建设若干举措的通知), document number 教师〔2025〕1号 (Teacher [2025] No. 1).

The notice outlines ten key measures to build a strong PE teacher workforce for primary and secondary schools:

1. **Clear goals**: By 2027, improve the quantity and structure of PE teacher teams with better teaching quality; by 2035, form a comprehensive mechanism aligned with education modernization and building an education powerhouse.

2. **Strict ethics**: Incorporate educator spirit and Chinese sports spirit into PE teacher training; enforce strict standards for professional ethics with "zero tolerance" for violations.

3. **Increase training**: Expand PE education major enrollment in free teacher education programs and "Excellent Teacher Plan"; strengthen practical training; encourage universities to offer PE micro-majors for non-PE students.

4. **Optimize recruitment**: Set PE teacher staffing standards at no higher than a teacher-student ratio of 5:1 for primary schools, 6:1 for junior high, and 8:1 for senior high; recruit excellent retired athletes (especially football players) and veterans; require second-level athlete certificates for non-PE majors.

5. **Coordinate resources**: Establish monitoring mechanisms, promote "county-managed, school-employed" reform, teacher rotation, cross-school teaching, and township walk-in teaching for rural small schools.

6. **Enhance capabilities**: Establish training bases, optimize the "National Training Plan," focus on football, basketball, volleyball, and traditional Chinese sports training; implement AI-empowered education to boost digital literacy.

7. **Implement coach positions**: Each county should set at least one full-time coach position; recruit retired athletes with first-level athlete certification; allow mutual job transfers between coaches and PE teachers with proper qualifications.

8. **Improve evaluation and incentives**: Count PE teachers' work in recess activities, fitness monitoring, after-school training, competitions, and walk-in teaching toward workload; ensure equal treatment in titles, benefits, and awards as other subjects; guarantee a certain proportion of PE teachers in teaching awards.

9. **Strengthen organizational leadership**: Include PE teacher team building in the supervision and evaluation of county compulsory education quality; strengthen full-time PE teaching researcher teams.

10. **Ensure funding**: Increase school sports funding, include PE work costs in annual budgets, and guide social funds to support primary and secondary school sports.

The notice was published on the Ministry of Education's official website (www.moe.gov.cn) on January 24, 2025.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 4: 乔锦忠、钟秉林等：2020—2035年我国义务教育阶段资源配置研究 ---
URL: http://www.esidea.bnu.edu.cn/zcfg/125469.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage presents a research study by Beijing Normal University scholars 乔锦忠 and 钟秉林 titled "专家观点" (Expert Opinion), published on December 22, 2021, predicting compulsory education (义务教育) school-age population changes and their impact on educational resource allocation in China during 2020-2035.

BACKGROUND AND METHODOLOGY: The study was conducted under the guidance of China's "中国教育现代化2035" (China's Education Modernization 2035) plan, which aims for quality and balanced development of compulsory education. The researchers used the Leslie matrix cohort-component method (队列要素法) and field interviews, based on sixth census data, 1% population sampling data, and recent birth data. They modeled populations by urban/rural classification, gender, and age, integrating factors including birth rates, mortality, migration, and fertility policies. The study defines compulsory education age as 6-15 years old.

KEY FINDINGS ON STUDENT NUMBERS:
1. Compulsory education student numbers will experience a short 4-year slow increase followed by an 11-year rapid decline. Student enrollment will rise from 140 million in 2020 to a peak of about 146 million in 2024, then decline to about 110 million by 2035—a drop of approximately 30 million from 2020 levels.
2. By around 2031, urban (城区) compulsory education students will exceed town (镇区) students, marking the overall transition to a city-education-dominated era. Rural students will decline to 16.23 million by 2035 (down about 10.26 million from 2020), mostly at the primary level.
3. Junior high enrollment peaks in 2029 at 50.55 million; primary school enrollment peaks in 2024 at 99.15 million.
4. Education urbanization rates exceed resident population urbanization rates (2017 rates: junior high 85.52%, primary 72.50%), so the study used enrollment-based urbanization rates rather than household registration-based rates for resource planning.

SCHOOL INFRASTRUCTURE DEMAND:
1. National compulsory education school demand declines from 2020, reaching only 140,700 schools by 2035 (down 55,200 from 2020).
2. Rural school demand drops sharply—rural primary schools decline to 35,500 by 2035 (a surplus/idle of 37,300 schools); rural junior high demand stays relatively stable at 11,400-14,200.
3. Urban areas need to build 4,000 new primary schools by 2026 (peak year) and 4,000 new junior highs by 2030 (peak year).
4. Rural teaching points (教学点) will continue declining.

TEACHER DEMAND:
Using 2019 teacher-student ratios (primary 16.85:1, junior high 12.88:1), teacher demand peaks at 9.51 million in 2025, then declines to 7.29 million by 2035. Compared with 2020, by 2035 there will be a surplus of ~1.50 million primary school teachers (~149.55万) and ~372,600 junior high teachers (37.26万). Primary school teachers peak at 5.88 million in 2024; junior high teachers peak at 3.92 million in 2029.

FINANCIAL/EXPENDITURE DEMAND:
Assuming 4% GDP growth (2020-2035) and constant education cost indices, per-student public budget education expenditures will rise: primary by ~10,000 yuan/student and junior high by ~14,000 yuan/student by 2035 (under unified urban-rural standards). Urban areas require far more additional funding than rural areas (urban needs annual increases of ~555.25 billion yuan vs. rural total increase of only 629.80 billion yuan over 15 years). Implementing unified urban-rural per-student funding standards would add only about 0.75%-1.00% to total education expenditure.

POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS (sections 六 and 七 were listed but content not provided in the page): The study suggests scientifically planning school layouts, appropriately raising educational standards to lower teacher-student ratios and class sizes, timely supplementing excellent teachers, and coordinating optimization of teacher resources across preschool, childcare, and compulsory education stages to continuously improve teacher workforce structure.

The study notes limitations including variation in assumptions about total fertility rates and urbanization levels, and notes that richer provinces (like Sichuan, entering city-dominated education by 2029) will transition to urban education earlier than 2031, while poorer provinces will lag.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 5: 张现苓：基于学龄人口新格局的基础教育师资调配机制优化 ---
URL: https://www.cnaes.edu.cn/post/30158

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the Chinese Academy of Educational Sciences (中国教育科学研究院, cnaes.edu.cn) and presents a research article by Li Xincui (李新翠) and Zhang Xianling (张现苓) titled "基于学龄人口新格局的基础教育师资调配机制优化" (Optimizing Basic Education Teacher Allocation Mechanisms Based on the New Pattern of School-Age Population), published in the journal 《教育研究》(Educational Research) 2024, Issue 11 (time: 2025-01-06).

**Background and Research Question:**
China's population is entering a decline phase: the 7th National Population Census (2020) showed 12 million births with a total fertility rate (TFR) of about 1.3 and annual population growth of 0.53%; the 2021 birth rate was only 7.52‰ with 10.62 million births. Since TFR has fallen below the "very low fertility" threshold of 1.5 (from which recovery is difficult), the paper argues that optimizing teacher allocation mechanisms is essential for achieving educational quality and the strategy of becoming an education power (教育强国).

**Methodology:**
- Used the cohort-component method (队列要素法) to predict school-age population for 2020–2050 across all basic education stages (preschool through high school), using 7th census data as baseline.
- Key parameters: baseline population from census, TFR assumed to fluctuate between 1.2–1.3, life expectancy projected using UN medium-high growth assumption with Coale-Demaney West model life tables, sex ratio at birth held at 111.3, urbanization set to reach target with 2035 urban rate (noted as 35% in text) with linear change.
- Predicted teacher demand using fixed student-teacher ratios (preschool 14:1, primary 14:1, junior high 13:1, senior high 12:1), considering policies of fiscal personnel reduction.
- Estimated teacher retirement based on 2021《中国教育统计年鉴》data (female teachers retire at 55, male at 60).
- Model validation: prediction errors for ages 3–17 were all within 10% absolute error (most within 3%), classified as high-precision by MAPE standards.

**Key Findings on School-Age Population:**

1. **Preschool children (学龄前儿童)** follow a "down-stable-down" trend: from over 52 million in 2020, falling rapidly to under 29 million by 2030, stabilizing around 28 million, then declining again after 2040 to about 25 million by 2050. Rural areas decline much faster (2020–2030 decline of 63.76% vs. 33.72% for urban).

2. **Compulsory education-age children (义务教育适龄儿童, ages 6–14)** follow a "stable-down-stable" trend: about 160 million through 2025, then declining to ~85 million in 2030–2040 (a drop of over 45%). Primary school-age children stay above 100 million until 2025, drop below 60 million around 2035 (due to post-2017 decline in births after the two-child policy effect faded). Junior high age children peak at 55.85 million in 2026 before declining. Urban areas increase first (peak 101.96 million in 2024) then decline to 62.34 million by 2050; rural areas drop from 63.92 million in 2020 to 18.08 million in 2039, then slightly recover to 23.26 million by 2050.

3. **Senior high school age population** rises then falls: from 44.27 million in 2020, peaking at 55.81 million in 2029, then declining sharply in 2033–2038 (from 51.37 million to 32.43 million, a 36.88% drop), stabilizing around 28 million by 2050.

**Teacher Allocation Policy Recommendations:**

1. **Preschool teachers:** Teacher-student ratio was 15.06:1 in 2021 (near OECD levels of 14.4–15.3:1). Focus on optimizing existing stock until 2025; after 2040 (when teachers enter retirement peak, since 74.73% of teachers were under 35 in 2021), shift to incremental allocation.

2. **Primary school teachers:** Ratio was 16.33:1 in 2021 (below the national standard of 19:1). Need long-term stock optimization before 2040; require incremental allocation after 2040 due to mass retirements (peak retirement in 2045). Demand peaks in 2025 due to two/three-child policy effects. Rural primary school-age children fall by over 70% from 2020 to 2036.

3. **Junior high teachers:** Ratio was 12.64:1 in 2021 (slightly above national standard). From 2021: ratio of 12.83:1 (urban) and 11.40:1 (rural). Stock optimization the focus through 2025; demand declines most sharply 2030–2035; incremental demand grows again after 2035, especially 2045–2050. In 2030, urban areas need significant incremental allocation while rural is roughly balanced.

4. **Senior high teachers:** Ratio was 12.84:1 in 2021. Focus on sustained incremental allocation; demand peaks around 2029–2030 (peak school-age population); largest incremental demand in 2025, lowest around 2035.

**Overall Conclusion:** Junior high school and below must focus on optimizing existing teacher stock, while senior high school teachers need continuous incremental allocation. The paper provides systematic, longest-horizon projections (to 2050, coinciding with China's second centenary goal) with concrete policy implications for optimizing teacher resource allocation amid demographic decline.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"第七次全国人口普查数据显示，2020年度出生人口规模为1200万，总和生育率约为1.3，人口年均增长率为0.53%","2021年，我国人口出生率仅为7.52‰，出生人口规模为1062万，再创新低","2021年，全国幼儿园教师74.73%为35岁以下，45岁以上教师仅占25.27%，因此，2040年后才进入退休高峰年段","农村小学适龄儿童已经进入下行通道，未来十余年降幅明显，从2020年的4296万降至2036年的1187万，降幅达到70%以上","总体而言，初中及以下学段教师重在存量优化，高中教师则需要持续配置增量"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 6: 高中生体育锻炼习惯与体质健康水平的相关性研究 ---
URL: https://pdf.hanspub.org/ces2025133_273094782.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a peer-reviewed research article published in *Creative Education Studies* (创新教育研究), March 2025, by Lei Xin, Fan Zhengyao, and Fan Yunxiang (Hunan Normal University and First Furong Middle School, Changsha, Hunan, China). The study investigates the correlation between physical activity habits and physical fitness levels among high school students.

**Methodology:** The researchers used the Physical Exercise Habits Assessment Scale and the Physical Activity Rating Scale (PARS-3) to survey 1,216 high school students from five schools in Hunan Province (Yiyang Nanxian No.1, Lida, Yueyang Pingjiang No.3, Shaoyang Chuangxin, and Loudi Mingde). Of 1,400 distributed questionnaires, 1,330 were returned (95.0% response rate) with 1,216 valid (91.4% validity). Sample included 736 males and 480 females across grades 10-12 (428, 452, and 336 respectively).

**Key Results:**
- Physical activity habits were diversified: 35.5% had established stable habits, 34.9% were in an unstable initial stage, and 29.6% had poor/missing habits with insufficient exercise duration and intensity
- Physical fitness overall average was 76.31 ± 11.699 (passing range, near-normal distribution): 11.2% excellent, 24.3% good, 55.9% passing, 8.6% failing
- Correlation coefficient between physical activity habits and overall physical fitness score was 0.415** (moderate correlation); exercise volume correlated at 0.428**
- Exercise volume averaged 29.53 ± 26.968 (medium intensity); 49.3% of students were in the fluctuating/low-volume range
- Students showed high exercise frequency but relatively low intensity and short duration per session
- Females scored higher on fitness (77.84) than males (75.32)

**Conclusions:** Physical activity habits and physical fitness levels are significantly positively correlated. "Physical activity life integration" (体育生活化) and "persistence in physical activity" (持续坚持) are key factors for improving fitness. Recommendations include building personalized exercise guidance, strengthening physical education teacher training with short-duration high-intensity workout options, and establishing comprehensive physical fitness monitoring systems. The study is funded by the Hunan Provincial Basic Education Teaching Reform Research Project (Y20230723).

## Policy Background (3 sections)

**1. Evolution of daily physical activity time policy (5 stages):**
- Stage 1 (1950s): 1951 State Council decision restricted student activities, recommending 1-1.5 hours of daily physical/recreational activity due to excessive academic workloads threatening health.
- Stage 2 (1978-1990s): After Cultural Revolution, 1978 notice required average 1 hour daily organized exercise; 1990 《学校体育工作条例》 legally mandated 1 hour daily physical activity (including PE classes).
- Stage 3 (2005-2011): Multiple documents (2005, 2006, 2007, 2009 《全民健身条例》, 2011 Government Work Report) clarified that the 1 hour must be on-campus time.
- Stage 4 (2020-present): Shift to requirement of 2 hours daily comprehensive activity (can be on or off campus).
- Stage 5: The 2-hour requirement targeting primary and secondary students (not university students).

**Key policy milestones for the 2-hour requirement:**
- October 2020: 中办国办 document first mentioned ensuring 2 hours daily (1 hour on campus + 1 hour off campus).
- Early 2024: Ministry of Education included "2-hour daily exercise pilot for compulsory education students" in annual work priorities.
- September 26, 2024: Vice Minister of Education 王嘉毅 announced the 2-hour requirement (one PE class daily + 1 hour after-class exercise).
- December 27, 2024: MOE held national school sports reform symposium in Anhui.
- January 2025: 《教育强国建设规划纲要(2024—2035年)》 formally required "中小学生每天综合体育活动时间不低于2小时".

**2. School sports as key content of education power construction:** School sports has political character (part of five-fold education), people's character (affects family well-being), and strategic character (national talent competition). Countries like US, UK, Finland, Australia, Japan are all strengthening school sports.

**3. New education ecosystem creating conditions:** Education structure reform, quality improvements (91.1% preschool enrollment, 95.7% nine-year compulsory education completion, 60.2% higher education enrollment), and "double reduction" policy (双减) freeing up student time. 92.7% of schools conduct arts/sports activities; 90%+ of students voluntarily participate in after-school services.

## Practical Basis (3 sections)

**1. Addressing chronic weakness in student physical fitness:** Despite 4 high-level policy documents over ~40 years (2007, 2012, 2016, 2020), student fitness hasn't fundamentally improved. 2023 national tests showed: 87.1% pass rate (down 2.9 percentage points from 2021), 35.3% excellent rate (down 3.3 points), 12.9% fail rate. Chongqing survey: 64.1% of students exercise less than 1 hour after school; nearly 60% exercise less than 30 minutes daily. Students with 1+ hour daily exercise had 27.4% excellent fitness rate vs 17.7% for those with insufficient time.

**2. Cultivating independent exercise habits:** 2018 national monitoring shows only 28.4% of 4th graders and 18.6% of 8th graders have genuine exercise habits. Eastern regions highest (32.4%, 20.7%), central regions lowest (25.7%, 16.3%). Urban students higher than rural. Longer immersive exercise time helps build habits.

**3. Local reform experiences:** Multiple provinces implemented reforms before national policy:
- Beijing (2021): daily PE class policy; 2024: 15-minute recess periods.
- Shanghai (2023): 2 hours daily exercise, 5 PE classes/week for primary, 4 for middle school.
- Yunnan (2024): 2 daily eye exercises, 30-min big recess, 15-min recess minimum.
- Tianjin (2024): morning/afternoon 30-min big recess, ensure 1 hour on + 1 hour off campus.
- Anhui (2024): daily PE class, two 30-min big recesses.
- Inner Mongolia (2025): daily PE class for compulsory education, 2/week for high school.
- Jiangsu (2025): "2•15 Special Action" — 2 hours activity, 15-min recess.
- Sichuan (2025): 2-hour requirement including PE class, recess, after-school services, and off-campus activity.

## Implementation Considerations (5 sections)

**1. Correctly understanding reform significance:** Vice Minister 王嘉毅 stated: "School sports appears to be a sports issue, but is actually a deep educational issue... 2 hours is not just a time issue, but a systematic reform that pulls one thread and moves the whole web, involving teaching, activities, competition, training, teachers, venues, evaluation, and support."

**2. Systematic structural arrangement:** 2 hours is "comprehensive" activity (can combine PE class + recess + big recess + after-school service + off-campus). Optimal structure: daily PE class + 15-min recesses + two 30-min big recesses + 1 hour after-school sports (=~3 hours on campus). Alternative: daily PE class + two 30-min big recesses + 1 hour after-school (=~2.5 hours). Requires reducing excess cultural class time, strengthening conditions, and scientific activity design.

**3. Integrated design of activity content:** 2 hours should be designed as one system connecting teaching, exercise, and competition along a time continuum, avoiding fragmented approaches. Key points: follow curriculum standards, extend classroom teaching into extracurricular activities, apply skills in daily life, and monitor/regulate exercise load across the week.

**4. Strengthening condition guarantees:** Teacher needs nearly double (e.g., PE classes increase from 4 to 5/week for grades 1-2, 3 to 5/week for grades 3-9). Solutions: expedite staffing quotas, train existing teachers as part-time PE teachers, recruit retired athletes and volunteers (e.g., Sichuan Tianfu New Area shared teacher system covering ~200 schools; Beijing #11 School with 20+ full-time and 80+ part-time PE teachers). Venue solutions: reserve space in new schools, develop "micro-playgrounds" in corners/rooftops/underground, establish venue sharing mechanisms with public facilities (e.g., Chongqing Coral Luneng Primary School's eight-theme sports park; Guizhou's corridor "micro-playgrounds").

**5. Sports injury risk prevention and handling:** Schools must not "give up eating for fear of choking" — continuing activities despite possible minor injuries. Requirements: use certified equipment, establish equipment safety ledgers, strengthen activity management (pre-activity equipment checks, decomposition of difficult movements, adequate warm-up), conduct risk training, improve insurance systems (school liability insurance, no-fault insurance, sports injury insurance, accident insurance), and use third-party mediation. 《中华人民共和国民法典》 (Civil Code) provides legal support for handling sports injury disputes.

**Conclusion:** School sports is a weak link in education power construction. Going forward, it must take comprehensive deepening of reform as its overall tone, enhancing student physical health as the overall goal, and the 2-hour comprehensive activity as the overall grip, promoting high-quality school sports development to cultivate fully-developed new-era talents.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from the Chinese Ministry of Education (moe.gov.cn) addresses the ongoing efforts to improve student physical health in Chinese schools. It emphasizes that student physical fitness monitoring matters not just for the data, but as a reminder that health education is a systematic project extending beyond physical education classes.

The article begins by citing President Xi Jinping's statement on youth health: "少年强、青年强则中国强" (If the youth are strong, China is strong), emphasizing that strength includes not only academics and creativity but also physical health and athletic spirit.

Historically, schools faced rising rates of "小胖墩" (chubby/overweight children) and "小眼镜" (children with glasses). Many schools treated physical education inadequately—shortened class hours, lagging activity organization, inadequate facilities, and weak teaching staff. A shared expectation developed among parents, schools, and society to establish a health-first educational philosophy and integrate sports with education.

Recent policy efforts have yielded results. The Eighth National Student Physical Fitness and Health Survey (jointly conducted by the Ministry of Education, General Administration of Sport, National Health Commission, and other agencies) showed overall improvement: students' height, weight, and chest circumference indicators improved; lung capacity rose; flexibility, strength, speed, and endurance improved; and malnutrition rates declined. The overall excellence rate of student physical fitness has trended upward.

These gains stem from schools deepening the integration of sports and education, advancing teaching reforms through the "health knowledge + basic motor skills + specialized motor skills" model, promoting "one school, one brand" initiatives, and enforcing mandatory physical education curriculum hours. However, challenges remain: high myopia rates, rising overweight/obesity rates, declining grip strength, and declining physical fitness among university students.

The article notes that youth health and school physical education have been incorporated into local government assessment indicators, and numerous relevant policy documents have been issued. Most recently, five ministries jointly issued "Opinions on Comprehensively Strengthening and Improving School Health and Health Education Work in the New Era" to systematize school health education content. The article concludes that building a comprehensive health education system requires both immediate action and long-term vision.
